findings.title: Saved-zone clean dispatches to the device when the active-map signal is blank — the "active map only" guard is permissive, not a refusal
findings.what_code_does: _handle_clean_saved_zone (2603-2612) and _handle_clean_saved_zones (2658-2667) resolve the active map, swallow any exception to None, then refuse only when `active_map_id is not None and str(active_map_id) != str(map_id)`. When get_active_map_id returns None the guard falls through and the zone is dispatched. get_active_map_id (rooms/room_discovery.py:43-84) returns None for any BLANK state — entity_helpers.BLANK_STATE_VALUES = {"", "unknown", "unavailable", "none", "null"} — and also when the entity is registered but has no state yet (boot/reload window). dispatch_zone_clean (dispatch/manager.py:86-107) explicitly does NOT send map_id ("the provider uses its own currently-loaded map"), so this service-layer check is the ONLY thing binding the geometry to a map.
findings.reproduction: Roborock S6. Adapter declares active_map = select.<id>_selected_map, whose state is the map NAME (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:163,190). Saved zone "under the couch" on map_id="Main floor", geometry [[0.20,0.30],[0.30,0.30],[0.30,0.40],[0.20,0.40]] -> rect [0.20,0.30,0.30,0.40]. Robot currently has "Upstairs" loaded, and the Roborock integration is mid-reload so the select is `unavailable`. Call clean_saved_zone(map_id="Main floor", zone_id=...). is_blank_state("unavailable") -> True -> active_map_id=None -> guard passes. dispatch_zone_clean takes cfg zone_coords=="device_mm", calls get_live_mapdata_obj (mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:330-358) which returns whatever MapData is in the Roborock integration's memory WITHOUT checking it is "Main floor", and normalized_rects_to_mm (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:102-131) fits the affine from THAT map's correspondences. Arithmetic: Main floor 60x60px @50mm/px origin (-1000,-1000) -> x0 = -1000 + 0.20*3000 = -400 mm, x1 = -1000 + 0.30*3000 = -100 mm; Upstairs 100x80px @50mm/px origin (2000,500) -> x0 = 2000 + 0.20*5000 = 3000 mm, x1 = 3500 mm. Same stored rect, two rectangles ~3.4 m apart. The residual check in normalized_rects_to_mm only validates the affine's self-consistency, so the wrong-map fit passes cleanly and the robot cleans a different physical area (on Roborock, a different floor). On Eufy the normalized rect is shipped verbatim and the fork de-normalizes against its own loaded map — same wrong-area outcome.
findings.user_impact: The vacuum cleans a physically different area from the one the user named and tapped, with no error and no way to tell from the response (it returns {cleaned: true}). Requires the active-map entity to be blank (integration reload, cloud hiccup, HA restart window), so the common path is fine — but the failure is physical and silent, and an automation firing shortly after HA start sits exactly in that window.
findings.guards_checked: (a) The `str(active_map_id) != str(map_id)` comparison itself — correct when a value exists, does nothing when None. (b) dispatch_zone_clean's degenerate-rect check (dispatch/manager.py:110-118) — checks side length only, not which map. (c) normalized_rects_to_mm's 50mm residual validation — validates the affine fit, not the map identity; a wrong-map affine is perfectly self-consistent. (d) get_live_mapdata_obj takes map_id as a parameter but only uses it to resolve the live image ENTITY, never to verify the returned MapData is that map. (e) The job path's map_mismatch guard (jobs/job_monitor.py:172, 254) is identically permissive (`selected_map_id_n and active_map_id_n and ...`), so this is the systemic permissive default, NOT a forgotten sibling.
findings.doc_checked: docs/advanced/03-services.md:75 and :140/:153 — states the two clean services are "active-map-guarded (a zone's geometry is only valid on its own map)" unconditionally; docs/dev/frontend/backend-contract-and-data-shapes.md:71 — "requires the zone's map to be the active map"; docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §6 (the "one hard rule"). All three state the requirement with no indeterminate-map exception, so code and doc diverge.
findings.brands_affected: Both. Roborock is more exposed: map_id is the vendor map NAME read off a select entity that goes `unavailable` whenever the upstream integration reloads, and the wrong-map projection can land on a different FLOOR.

findings.title: delete_saved_zone performs no reference check; run-profile and queue `zone` steps keep the dead id and are silently dropped at run time while the UI still lists them
findings.what_code_does: _handle_delete_saved_zone (2539-2554) pops the zone from map_bucket['saved_zones'] and saves. It scans nothing else. Saved-zone ids are referenced from a second persisted store: queue_breaks / run-profile steps of the form {"type": "zone", "zone_ids": [...]} (core/manager.py:1736, 1835). ProfileManager.normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:798-808) keeps the ids verbatim and documents that "existence ... [is] enforced at dispatch". That enforcement is a silent skip: MapManager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1870-1883) `continue`s on a missing zone, and RunPlan (planning/run_plan.py:866-872) does `if not rects: continue` — dropping the entire phase.
findings.reproduction: Map has saved zones sz_A ("under the couch") and sz_B ("by the stove"). User builds a queue: Kitchen -> zone step [sz_A, sz_B] -> Bedroom (add_queue_zone, core/manager.py:1719). (1) Delete sz_B. Next run: _resolve_saved_zone_rects returns 1 rect; the phase dispatches ONE zone. The user's saved sequence silently cleans half of what it says. (2) Delete sz_A as well. rects == [] -> run_plan.py:871 `continue` -> the zone phase never enters the plan at all; the run goes Kitchen -> Bedroom. Meanwhile get_queue_steps (core/manager.py:1632-1678) rebuilds the step list straight from queue_breaks and still returns the zone step (normalize is shape-only), so the card's queue preview keeps showing it. The phase-runner's zone_timing snapshot (jobs/phase_runner.py:355-370) records zone_ids including the dead ids with zone_names falling back to the raw id string.
findings.user_impact: A saved run silently stops doing part of what the user built, and the UI keeps advertising the step that no longer runs. There is no warning at delete time and no reason code — the divergence is only discoverable by watching the robot. Non-edge: deleting a zone is a normal one-tap card action (docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §8 lists delete in the shipped Wave 3b UX).
findings.guards_checked: (a) normalize_run_profile_steps — validates shape only, explicitly defers existence to dispatch. (b) _resolve_saved_zone_rects — the deferred-to enforcer; it skips rather than reports (its own docstring admits "Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped"). (c) run_plan.py:871 `if not rects: continue` — drops the phase with no marker on the plan. (d) dispatch_zone_clean's `if not zones: raise` (dispatch/manager.py:108) would have surfaced it, but run_plan drops the phase before dispatch is ever reached. (e) learned_zones is NOT corrupted — ids are timestamp-minted and never reused, so a later zone cannot inherit a deleted zone's learning.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §5 (delete_saved_zone) and §10 (Invalidation) — neither mentions reference cleanup or a refuse-if-referenced rule; docs/dev/07-queue-engine.md and docs/dev/30-phase-runner.md describe the zone step but not the dangling-id case. The behaviour is undocumented in either direction, so this is not a documented design choice.
findings.brands_affected: Both — the zone step and its resolver are brand-agnostic.

findings.title: The `map_version` re-map invalidation the design doc specifies as the zone's safety key does not exist anywhere in the codebase
findings.what_code_does: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 declares SavedZone carries `"map_version": ...  # invalidation key (§6)`, and §10 states "Saved zones are keyed to the map version. A genuine re-map changes the room_pixels raster -> the stored geometry no longer means the same thing -> the map's saved zones invalidate". _create_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:1406-1415, called from my range at 2490) mints exactly {id, name, geometry, area_m2, room_number, kind, created_at, updated_at} — no map_version. `grep -rn map_version` across custom_components/, src/ and tests/ returns ZERO hits. Nothing stamps it, nothing checks it, and neither clean handler consults any freshness signal before dispatching.
findings.reproduction: Eufy or Roborock. 1) Save zone "under the couch" on map "Main floor": geometry stored as normalized [[0.20,0.30]..[0.30,0.40]]. 2) User re-runs a full mapping scan (or the robot auto-remaps after furniture changes). The new raster has different extents, so the same physical couch now sits at normalized ~[0.26,0.24]..[0.36,0.33]. The map_id (Eufy numeric id / Roborock map name) is unchanged, so the SAME map bucket and the SAME saved_zones dict are reused. 3) Tap the zone -> clean_saved_zone -> rect [0.20,0.30,0.30,0.40] is projected onto the NEW map's frame -> the robot cleans a region offset by ~6% of map width/height from the couch. No invalidation, no warning, no stale flag. 4) The stored area_m2/room_number are equally stale and are NOT recomputed: _backfill_saved_zone_area (1431-1471) only touches zones where `area_m2 is None`, so a zone sized against the pre-remap raster keeps its old number forever and continues feeding zone ETA (core/manager.py:3643-3665) and zone learning.
findings.user_impact: Every saved zone on a re-mapped floor silently points at the wrong physical spot, and the design's own stated defence against exactly this was never built. This is the direct failure of "survives a re-import": the edit does not survive, and nothing tells the user it stopped being valid. It is also irreversible from the UI — the only repair is delete + redraw every zone, and there is no signal telling the user which zones need it.
findings.guards_checked: (a) _backfill_saved_zone_area (1431-1439) — the only self-heal path; gated on `area_m2 is None`, so it never revisits a stale-but-populated value. (b) The active-map guard in the clean handlers — checks WHICH map, never WHEN the geometry was authored; a re-map keeps the same map_id so the guard passes. (c) created_at/updated_at are stamped but no consumer compares them to any map timestamp. (d) map_bucket['metadata']['last_rebuild'] (maps/map_manager.py:203) exists and would be a usable version signal — no saved-zone code reads it.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 (SavedZone schema, `map_version` line) and §10 (Invalidation) — the doc specifies the mechanism as built-in to the data model; docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §8 storage keys list makes no mention of it either. Code/doc divergence: the doc describes a guarantee that has no implementation.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: create_saved_zone files area_m2 + room_number from whatever raster is live when the active map is indeterminate, and that wrong value can never be corrected
findings.what_code_does: Lines 2497-2510 compute membership when `active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)` — i.e. an INDETERMINATE active map is treated as a match (the comment at 2496 says so: "Indeterminate active map -> compute"). manager.async_get_map_data_dict(vacuum_entity_id=...) at 2504 takes NO map_id: it always returns the currently live map's data. So on the None branch the zone's size and room filing are computed from a raster that may belong to a completely different map, then written to zone['area_m2'] / zone['room_number'] and persisted at 2512.
findings.reproduction: Eufy, two maps ("1" = downstairs, "2" = upstairs). Robot has map 2 loaded; the active-map sensor is `unknown` during the post-restart window (entity_helpers.BLANK_STATE_VALUES). User creates a zone on map "1" from the card's map-1 view. active_map_id=None -> guard passes -> zone_membership runs against map 2's room_pixels raster -> zone['area_m2'] = e.g. 3.4 (map-2 metres per pixel over map-2 dims) and zone['room_number'] = 7 (a map-2 room id that may not even exist on map 1). Both persist. Now the correction paths: _backfill_saved_zone_area (1434-1439) selects only zones with `area_m2 is None` — this zone is skipped forever; _handle_set_saved_zone_room (2557-2576) can fix room_number but writes nothing to area_m2. The wrong area then feeds _zone_ids_estimate_seconds (core/manager.py:3643-3665) and the zone-learning area fallback, and phase_runner._saved_zone_area_sum (jobs/phase_runner.py:382-401) folds it into the learned record.
findings.user_impact: A zone shows the wrong m² in the card list, is filed under a room from another map, and every ETA derived from it is wrong — permanently, with no UI path to fix the size. Needs the active-map signal blank at authoring time, so the common path is unaffected; the damage is that it is silent AND unrepairable rather than that it is likely.
findings.guards_checked: (a) The `active_map_id is None or ...` condition — the permissive half is the defect. (b) The outer try/except at 2497/2509 — catches failures, not wrongness; a successful compute against the wrong map raises nothing. (c) _backfill_saved_zone_area's identical guard at 1449 — same permissive None branch, so the self-heal path can also write wrong-map values (and cannot overwrite one already written). (d) set_saved_zone_room — repairs room_number only.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md, "Wave 2 (2026-07-02)" note — records the map-mismatch review finding and states the fix as "only compute when map_id == the active map (get_active_map_id), else leave None". The shipped code additionally computes when the active map is UNKNOWN, which is not what the doc says was fixed. Also §4 (room_number filing) and §3 (area_m2 "computed from map dims at author time").
findings.brands_affected: Eufy only — async_get_map_data_dict is the Eufy-only coordinator accessor (degrades to None elsewhere per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md Wave 2), so on Roborock both fields simply stay None.

findings.title: create_custom_layout force-flips segmentation_mode to "custom" with no record of the prior mode; delete only restores "cv" when zero layouts remain, so create-then-delete strands the user on a layout they never chose
findings.what_code_does: _handle_create_custom_layout sets `map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "custom"` unconditionally at 2346, discarding the previous value. _handle_delete_custom_layout restores "cv" only inside the `else` branch at 2429-2432 — i.e. only when NO layouts remain. When any layout remains it reassigns active to `sorted(remaining, key=name)[0]` (2423-2428) and leaves the mode at "custom". The pair is asymmetric: create always mutates the mode, delete conditionally restores it.
findings.reproduction: Install that has a legacy `custom_segments` store and segmentation_mode == "cv". First touch runs _migrate_custom_layouts (1483-1528), which mints layout cl_LEGACY named "Custom", sets it active, and deliberately does NOT change segmentation_mode — so the map is in CV mode with one dormant layout. User now: (1) calls create_custom_layout(name="Test") -> cl_NEW minted + activated, mode forced to "custom"; (2) decides against it and calls delete_custom_layout(cl_NEW). `layouts` still contains cl_LEGACY, so remaining is non-empty -> active_custom_layout_id = cl_LEGACY and segmentation_mode STAYS "custom". Final state: the map renders cl_LEGACY's authored segments, links and companion anchors instead of the CV segmentation the user was on before step (1). map_source.build_furnished_render (mapping/map_source.py:103-107) also flips on, so any furnished art on cl_LEGACY starts rendering. Undoing needs a separate set_segmentation_mode("cv") call that the delete response does not hint at (it returns segmentation_mode: "custom").
findings.user_impact: Creating and then cancelling a layout silently changes what the map card renders — a different room-to-segment mapping, different mascot anchors, possibly a furnished art layer. Presentation-level only (room CLEAN dispatch keys off device room ids, not segmentation_mode — verified: the only non-mapping_services consumer of segmentation_mode is map_source.py:103), so it is not a wrong-clean, but it is a user-visible state change nobody asked for and it is not obviously reversible.
findings.guards_checked: (a) The `if map_bucket.get("active_custom_layout_id") == layout_id` branch at 2422 — only asks whether the DELETED layout was active, never whether the mode was custom before any layout existed. (b) _handle_set_segmentation_mode's soft-select (1342-1345) — helps the opposite direction (custom with no active layout), not this one. (c) No prior-mode field is stored anywhere in the bucket, so restoring is not merely un-wired — the information is destroyed at 2346. (d) `remaining[0].get("id")` — additionally yields None if a layout dict lost its "id" key, leaving active=None while mode stays "custom".
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:755 (create: "then flip segmentation_mode to custom") and :757 (delete: "if none remain, set active_custom_layout_id = null and flip segmentation_mode back to cv"). Each half is documented; the doc never addresses the combination, and §10.1:648 claims "Flipping cv -> custom -> cv returns each segment set untouched" — true of the stores, but the MODE itself does not round-trip through create/delete.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: Every handler in the block mints a persisted map bucket for an unknown map_id — including on the pure not-found and read-only clean paths
findings.what_code_does: All ten handlers open with ensure_map_bucket (2341, 2361, 2383, 2452, 2486, 2526, 2545, 2566, 2595, 2652), which setdefaults a full bucket into manager.data (maps/map_manager.py:17-28), followed by _migrate_saved_zones / _migrate_custom_layouts which setdefault further keys. This happens BEFORE the `zone_not_found` / `layout_not_found` / `map_not_active` early returns, and before the two clean handlers — which mutate nothing conceptually — do any work. The early returns skip async_save, so the phantom is in-memory at that moment; but manager.async_save() persists the whole blob (core/manager.py:803-805), so the next save from ANY handler in the integration writes the phantom bucket to .storage permanently.
findings.reproduction: Roborock. map_id is the vendor map NAME read from select.<id>_selected_map (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190: "reports the map NAME (\"Main floor\")"). The user has 6 saved zones and 2 custom layouts under data["maps"][vacuum]["Main floor"]. They rename the map to "Ground floor" in the Roborock app. The select's state becomes "Ground floor"; the card now passes map_id="Ground floor" to every call. clean_saved_zone -> ensure_map_bucket setdefaults a brand-new empty bucket under "Ground floor" -> _migrate_saved_zones writes saved_zones={} into it -> zone lookup misses -> returns {"cleaned": false, "reason": "zone_not_found"}. Every zone and layout is now unreachable (stranded under the old key) and a phantom empty bucket exists, which get_vacuum_maps_summary (maps/map_manager.py:87-100) reports as a real map with room_count 0. Simpler variant, no rename needed: any single service call with a typo'd map_id ("Kitchn") permanently adds that map to the vacuum's map list.
findings.user_impact: All saved zones and custom layouts for a floor appear to vanish after a vendor-side map rename, with no error and no migration path — the data is intact in .storage under the old key but unreachable through any service. Separately, phantom maps accumulate in the map summary from typos or stale ids. Both are directly the "does the edit land on the map it names / survive a re-import" failure: the geometry is filed under a free-form, user-renameable key with no identity layer.
findings.guards_checked: (a) ensure_map_bucket has no exists-only variant in use here — get_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:55-74) is the non-mutating reader and IS used elsewhere (core/manager.py:1865, 3650), so the read-only accessor exists and simply is not used by these handlers. (b) The `zone_not_found` / `layout_not_found` returns happen after the mutation, not before. (c) No migration or alias table keys buckets by anything other than the raw map_id string. (d) This is distinct from the known-lead entity-id-prefix HIGH: the mechanism here is bucket minting on unknown ids and the loss mode is rename-strands-geometry.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:22 (map bucket contents, written by mapping_services) and :48-50; docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:616 ("keyed at data[\"maps\"][<vacuum>][<map_id>]"); docs/dev/03-data-model.md. None of them state that map_id is stable across a vendor-side rename, and none document bucket creation as a side effect of a failed lookup.
findings.brands_affected: Both for the phantom-bucket mechanism. The rename trigger is Roborock-specific (map NAME as id); the Roborock select's state changing on an in-app rename is near-certain but is device behaviour I could not verify from source.

findings.title: Both clean handlers ignore the zone's `kind`, so a zone saved with any non-"clean" kind is still dispatched as a clean
findings.what_code_does: CREATE_SAVED_ZONE_SCHEMA accepts `vol.Optional("kind"): cv.string` with no allow-list (453); _handle_create_saved_zone passes it through (2483) and _create_saved_zone persists it verbatim (1412). Neither _handle_clean_saved_zone (2614-2628) nor _handle_clean_saved_zones (2672-2698) reads zone['kind'] — they take the geometry's bbox and dispatch it unconditionally. `kind` has no consumer anywhere in custom_components/ or src/.
findings.reproduction: Call eufy_vacuum.create_saved_zone with name="cat bowls", kind="no_go", geometry=[...] (the service is documented in docs/advanced/03-services.md and the field is described as "reserved for future kinds"). The zone is stored with kind="no_go". Call clean_saved_zone on it -> rect derived, dispatch_zone_clean sends it -> the robot drives into and cleans the region the user labelled as a keep-out.
findings.user_impact: Latent today: no UI produces a non-"clean" kind, so only a direct service call reaches this. It matters because the field is publicly accepted, publicly documented as extensible, and the failure mode when someone uses it is physical rather than an error. Either reject unknown kinds at the schema or gate dispatch on kind == "clean".
findings.guards_checked: (a) The schema's cv.string — no vol.In allow-list. (b) `(kind or "clean").strip() or "clean"` at 1412 — normalises empty to "clean" but passes any other string through. (c) dispatch_zone_clean — receives only rects, so it cannot see kind. (d) Card-side: src/actions/saved-zones.js:43-54 forwards `kind` if the caller supplies one and never sets it itself.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 (`"kind": str, # "clean" (default); reserved for future kinds`) and §12 Non-goals ("Not map editing (no-go zones, virtual walls) — the app owns that"). The doc reserves the field without stating that dispatch ignores it.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: Zone size limits are not enforced at author time, contradicting the doc — an un-cleanable zone can be saved and only fails when the user taps clean
findings.what_code_does: _handle_create_saved_zone validates the name (2479-2481) and lets the schema clamp coordinates, but performs no size check: the computed area_m2 (2507) is stored and never compared against the adapter's zone_min_area_m2 / zone_max_area_m2 capabilities. Those bounds are only applied inside dispatch_zone_clean (dispatch/manager.py:164-177), plus the near-zero-side check at 110-118.
findings.reproduction: Roborock (zone_min_area_m2 ~0.093 m² / 1 ft²). Draw a small box, e.g. normalized [[0.50,0.50],[0.52,0.50],[0.52,0.52],[0.50,0.52]] on a 6m-wide map -> 0.12m x 0.12m = 0.014 m². create_saved_zone succeeds and returns {saved: true}; the zone appears in the panel with its m² label. Every subsequent clean_saved_zone on it raises ValueError -> HomeAssistantError "a zone is too small (0.01 m²)" (mapping_services.py:2629-2630). In a MULTI-select batch it is worse: one undersized zone raises inside dispatch_zone_clean and aborts the whole batch, so none of the selected zones get cleaned.
findings.user_impact: A zone that can never be cleaned is savable and looks valid in the list. The failure is loud (an error toast) rather than silent, hence LOW — but it is discovered at the wrong moment, and in a batch it blocks the other zones too.
findings.guards_checked: (a) _saved_zone_coord / _SAVED_ZONE_POINT (429-455) — validates coordinate sanity and point count, not area. (b) dispatch_zone_clean's _MIN_SIDE=0.01 normalized check — a normalized-units floor, unrelated to the device's m² bounds. (c) Card side: no min/max area gate found in src/actions/saved-zones.js or src/bindings/saved-zones.js, so the doc's "enforced at author" is unmet on both server and client.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §9 Validation — "reject/auto-tile a too-big zone, block a too-small one ... Enforced at author + at clean-time", and §8 "the size/count limits gate here". Only the clean-time half exists.
findings.brands_affected: Both (Eufy 0.5-10 m per side, Roborock 1 ft²-3.05 m²), per the caps quoted in the _handle_clean_saved_zones docstring at 2641-2642.

clean_areas: _handle_clean_saved_zones batch atomicity (mapping_services.py:2669-2692) — the docstring claims "any missing / bad-geometry zone refuses the whole batch" and the code delivers: missing[] and bad[] accumulate across the whole loop and BOTH are checked before dispatch, so a partial batch can never reach the device. The `if not rects` third check is redundant-but-harmless. Verified claim, not assumed.

_handle_rename_custom_layout (2352-2371) and _handle_rename_saved_zone (2517-2536) — blank-name refusal (`str(...).strip()` then `if not name`) precedes every mutation; the not-found return precedes any write; updated_at is stamped; the returned dict is a copy (`dict(layout)` / `dict(zone)`) so the caller cannot mutate the store through the response. No `or`-coercion hazard (both values are non-empty strings by construction).

_handle_delete_custom_layout's furnished-art sweep (2400-2418) — collects BOTH home_art.art_variant and every rooms[*].art_variant before removing, so the whole-home art and per-room art files are swept together; `(map_bucket.get("image_variants") or {}).pop(...)` on an absent store is a harmless no-op on a throwaway dict; the OSError swallow is right for best-effort file removal since the store entry is popped regardless (no half-state where the record survives a deleted file).

Saved-zone geometry schema, _saved_zone_coord + _SAVED_ZONE_POINT (429-455) — rejects bool, non-numeric, NaN and inf (the orjson-nulls-NaN trap), clamps finite values to 0-1, rounds to 5dp, requires exactly 2 coords per point and >=3 points. The two Wave-1 review findings recorded in docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md are genuinely fixed; out-of-range or non-finite geometry cannot persist through create_saved_zone. This kills the whole class of coordinate-injection findings for this block.

Bbox derivation agreement — the polygon->rect arithmetic at 2614-2622 (singular), 2677-2686 (batch) and MapManager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1874-1882) are line-for-line identical, including the `len(p) == 2` filter and the `len(pts) < 3` floor. A zone cleaned ad-hoc and the same zone cleaned inside a run profile therefore produce the same rect. (It is a hand copy defended by a comment — the campaign's known risk shape — but the three copies have NOT drifted.)

Delete-active-layout reassignment is event-loop-atomic (2420-2432) — `layouts.pop(layout_id)`, the `active_custom_layout_id == layout_id` test and the reassignment sit in one synchronous block with no await between them, so a concurrent create_custom_layout or set_active_custom_layout cannot interleave to leave active pointing at a deleted layout. (The earlier awaits at 2396/2416 are before the pop, so they cannot open this gap either.) Per rule 3 this is a false-positive by construction, not a real race.

Orphaned room_number is handled correctly card-side (src/state/saved-zones.js:101-131) — savedZonesGrouped falls a zone back into the Unassigned group when its room_number is not a room on the current map (re-map or deleted room), so _handle_set_saved_zone_room accepting an arbitrary int (2573, schema only vol.Coerce(int)) cannot make a zone invisible or unreachable in the panel. I went looking for an unreachable-zone bug here and there isn't one.

Id minting (_generate_saved_zone_id 1376-1385, _generate_custom_layout_id 1364-1373) — second-resolution timestamp plus a `_2`, `_3` collision suffix, evaluated synchronously inside the synchronous _create_saved_zone / _create_layout helpers with no await between mint and insert. Two creates in the same second cannot collide, and no id is ever reused.

learned_zones is deliberately and correctly left alone by delete_saved_zone — ids are timestamp-minted and never recycled, so a future zone cannot inherit a deleted zone's learned timings; jobs/phase_runner.py:362-364 snapshots zone_names at run time precisely so a later rename/delete keeps the record readable. This one is right on purpose.

_handle_set_saved_zone_room (2557-2576) honours the documented filing-only contract — it writes room_number and updated_at and touches nothing else; no dispatch path reads room_number (verified across core/manager.py, planning/run_plan.py, dispatch/), matching docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §4.
not_examined: The actual device behaviour of a wrong-map zone dispatch (ZONE-C-1) — the coordinate arithmetic is proven from source but the physical outcome needs the hardware run.
Whether the Roborock select.<id>_selected_map state actually changes when a map is renamed in the vendor app (ZONE-C-6's realistic trigger) — near-certain but not verifiable from this repo.
zone_membership internals (mapping/map_source.py:320+) — the map-source layer is out of scope; I treated it as a black box returning {area_m2, room_number}.

dispatch_zone_clean's per-brand payload correctness beyond the map-selection question (Eufy verbatim-normalized vs Roborock device_mm) — I verified which map the conversion reads, not that the conversion itself is right.

_backfill_saved_zone_area (1420-1471) — read in full because it is the only self-heal for area_m2/room_number and therefore load-bearing for ZONE-C-3 and ZONE-C-4, but it sits outside the assigned 2327-2710 range and I did not audit it in its own right. Note it carries the SAME permissive `active_map_id is None -> compute` branch at 1449.
_handle_set_furnished_art_placement / _handle_set_furnished_render_mode / _handle_set_room_viewport (~1830-2100) — art placement is another reviewer's area.
The card's draw->save flow in src/bindings/saved-zones.js beyond the two specific checks I ran (room grouping, size gating).
Concurrency between these handlers and the map-source coordinator's writers into the same map bucket — the map-source layer is out of scope per the brief.

findings.title: Re-analysis rebinds the user's room links and manual segment adjustments onto positionally-reassigned segment ids
findings.what_code_does: _handle_analyze_map_image replaces the whole CV store with `map_bucket["image_segments"] = result` (line 1174) and touches nothing else. The two user-authored overlays that key off segment identity — `segment_room_links` ({segment_id: room_id}, written by _handle_set_segment_room_link) and `image_segment_adjustments` ({segment_id: {offset_x, offset_y, edge_*, vertex_moves}}, written by _handle_adjust_map_segment:1784) — survive verbatim and are re-attached to the NEW segment list on the next read (_build_segments_response:1074 injects room_id by id; _apply_segment_adjustments:769 looks up adj by id). The inline comment at 1181-1184 asserts these are "independent of the image-derived segments". They are not: they are keyed BY the image-derived ids. Segment identity is purely positional — adapters/eufy/segmentor.py assigns `segment_{N}` from a running counter (1289/1474) and then re-sorts the list by area descending (1414/1485), so id N means "the Nth largest blob in THIS image", not "this room". Nothing stamps an image fingerprint, analyzed_at, or dimensions onto either overlay, and nothing validates that a stored id still exists in the new store.
findings.reproduction: Map with CV segments ranked by area: segment_1 = Living (48,000 px), segment_2 = Kitchen (30,500 px), segment_3 = Bedroom (30,400 px), on a 600x400 image. User links segment_3 -> room 5 (Bedroom) and nudges it +40 px in x to correct a CV offset, so adjustments = {"segment_3": {offset_x: 40, ...}}. User later re-uploads a fresh dark export (bedroom door now open, bedroom blob = 30,600 px; kitchen unchanged at 30,500) and the card auto-runs analyze with force_reanalyze=true (src/bindings/map.js:1104). The area sort now yields segment_2 = Bedroom, segment_3 = Kitchen. On the next get_map_segments: links["segment_3"] = 5 injects room_id 5 onto the KITCHEN polygon, and adjustments["segment_3"] shifts the kitchen polygon +40 px (kitchen vertex x=210 -> 250, polygon_pct 35.0 -> 41.67). A second arithmetic variant: if the replacement image is 1200 px wide instead of 600, the stored +40 px offset is reapplied verbatim in the new pixel space, so the same nudge is now 3.33% of the map instead of 6.67% — the correction silently halves. vertex_moves are worse: _adjust_polygon_pixel:748 applies them by list INDEX, so vertex_moves[{index: 7, delta_y: -12}] authored against a 14-vertex polygon lands on whatever vertex 7 is in the new polygon, or is silently dropped when the new polygon has <=7 vertices.
findings.user_impact: The map overlay silently mislabels rooms after any re-analysis in which blob ordering shifts, and the mislabel is actuating, not cosmetic: tapping a segment polygon calls toggleRoomEnabled for the LINKED room (src/bindings/map.js:869-897 and 2135), so the user taps the polygon drawn over the kitchen and the integration enables the bedroom for the next clean — the vacuum then physically cleans a room the user did not point at. Manual geometry corrections are simultaneously re-applied to unrelated polygons. Nothing in the response marks a link or adjustment as stale, so there is no signal to relink and no way to tell which links are still valid.
findings.guards_checked: (a) `force_reanalyze` gate at 1100 — only decides whether to re-run, never clears the overlays; (b) _build_segments_response:1074 `if linked_room is not None` — a presence check on the LINK, not on whether the id still denotes the same region; (c) _apply_segment_adjustments:770 `if not seg_id or not isinstance(adj, dict)` — same, id-presence only; (d) _handle_adjust_map_segment:1749 `segment_not_found` — validates the id at WRITE time against the then-current store, and is never re-run after re-analysis; (e) _handle_set_segment_room_link's 1:1 enforcement — enforces uniqueness of the mapping, not its continued meaning; (f) the `translated_manual`/`edge_adjusted_manual` issue tags added at 813-820 mark that an adjustment was applied, not that it was applied to the right segment.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:639 and docs/dev/03-data-model.md:157 both state that re-running CV "re-segments and forces a relink (accepted)". No relink is forced or even suggested anywhere in the code path — links are silently retained, which is the opposite of what both docs describe. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:467 documents only the adjacent cross-SCOPE collision (a custom id colliding with a CV adjustment) and calls it latent; the same-scope re-analysis case is not covered. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:2.12 confirms `segment_id` is `segment_{N}`, a 1-based running index.
findings.brands_affected: Both. Eufy (eufy_cv_v1) is where re-analysis actually reshuffles ids; Roborock inherits the same read-time enrichment for any image_segments it holds.

findings.title: A failed or unavailable segmenter run overwrites the good cached segmentation with an empty available:False envelope and persists it
findings.what_code_does: Line 1172-1175 does `result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_run)` then unconditionally `map_bucket["image_segments"] = result` and `await manager.async_save()`. There is no check on `result.get("available")` and no rollback. The engine seam never raises: EufyCVSegmenter.segment_map_image wraps detect_room_segments in `except Exception` (segmenter_engines.py:280-291) and returns `_engine_unavailable(reason="engine_exception")`, and _engine_unavailable (segmenter_engines.py:429-440) returns a fully-formed dict with `available: False`, `image: None`, `segments: []`, `summary.segment_count: 0`. get_segmenter_engine(None) (segmenter_engines.py:391) also returns NoopSegmenter, which returns the same empty envelope for any adapter whose mapping block omits `segmenter_engine`. So every failure mode arrives as a well-formed EMPTY result that is written straight over the previously cached good segmentation and flushed to .storage.
findings.reproduction: Eufy map with 9 cached CV segments plus links and adjustments. User uploads a replacement dark PNG; the card writes it to the SAME path (`map_<map_id>_dark.png`, line 896 — deterministic, no versioning, no backup) and then auto-calls analyze with force_reanalyze=true (src/bindings/map.js:1095-1104). detect_room_segments raises on the new image (or scipy/Pillow are absent — the integration declares requirements=[] and probes them at runtime via image_runtime_capabilities). The engine returns {available: False, reason: "engine_exception", segments: []}; line 1174 replaces the 9-segment store with it and line 1175 persists. Second path, no bad image needed: any adapter with no `segmenter_engine` declared (noop_fallback) — a single analyze_map_image call wipes image_segments to {segments: []} with reason "noop".
findings.user_impact: All room polygons disappear from the map view (src/renderers/map.js:109 falls back to a placeholder when `!segmentsData.available`) and the cached segmentation is unrecoverable: the source PNG the segments were derived from was just overwritten at the same filename by the upload that triggered the analysis, so re-running analyze cannot reproduce the previous result. The user's `segment_room_links` and `image_segment_adjustments` survive as orphans and will be re-bound to whatever the next successful analysis produces (see IMAGE--1). The service returns the failure envelope, but the destruction has already been committed to .storage before the caller can react.
findings.guards_checked: (a) `if not force_reanalyze and map_bucket.get("image_segments")` at 1100 — a cache-hit gate, not a write guard, and the card always passes force_reanalyze=true; (b) `if not image_path` at 1125 — the only pre-flight abort, and it returns before touching the bucket, which shows the write-guard shape was available and simply not applied to the engine result; (c) the executor call at 1172 — the engine's own try/except means no exception ever reaches this frame, so "an exception would have skipped the write" does not hold; (d) `_build_segments_response` at 1184 — read-side only; (e) manager.async_save() — persists whatever it is given, there is no prior snapshot.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §2.12 ("Stored image_segments envelope") documents the success envelope and says _handle_analyze_map_image "then stamps analyzed_at"; it does not state that an unavailable result is also cached. docs/dev/03-data-model.md:150-157 calls image_segments "cached on the first analyze_map_image and treated as immutable from the UI" — an available:False overwrite contradicts that framing. docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1125 describes the two call sites as consuming "the canonical SegmentationResult and cache it", again with no unavailable-result carve-out.
findings.brands_affected: Both. Eufy via engine_exception / missing optional CV libs; Roborock and any adapter without a registered segmenter engine hits it on the very first analyze call via noop_fallback.

findings.title: The analyze cache-hit gate tests truthiness, so a cached FAILURE envelope is served as a valid cache forever
findings.what_code_does: `if not force_reanalyze and map_bucket.get("image_segments"):` treats any non-empty dict as a valid cache. The failure envelope written by IMAGE--2 is a non-empty dict ({available: False, reason: ..., segments: [], summary: {...}}), so it is truthy and satisfies the gate. The gate never inspects `available`, `reason`, or `segments`. This is the codebase's documented 'absent is not zero / truthiness eats a legitimate state' pattern: 'no usable segmentation' and 'a valid cached segmentation' are indistinguishable here.
findings.reproduction: scipy is missing at the time of the first analyze -> image_segments = {available: False, reason: "pipeline_unavailable", segments: []}. The user installs scipy and restarts HA. Any caller that invokes analyze_map_image without force_reanalyze (the default is False, ANALYZE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:355) — an automation, a script, Developer Tools, or any future card path — takes the cache branch at 1101 and returns the stale failure envelope with the old reason string. The segmenter is never retried; the only escape is knowing to pass force_reanalyze explicitly.
findings.user_impact: Analysis appears permanently broken with a stale, now-incorrect reason ('you're missing scipy') after the cause has been fixed. The card is immune today because both of its call sites hard-code force_reanalyze:true, so this bites service/automation callers and any future UI path that trusts the documented default.
findings.guards_checked: (a) `force_reanalyze` — the only escape hatch, and its default is False; (b) `available` is present in the stored envelope and would have made a correct gate, but is never read here; (c) _build_segments_response:1055 `base = map_bucket.get("image_segments") or {}` — the same truthiness treatment on the read side, so it does not filter the failure envelope either; (d) no TTL, analyzed_at check, or image-mtime comparison anywhere in the handler.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §2.12 and docs/dev/03-data-model.md:150-157 describe image_segments as a cache populated on the first analyze and re-run via force_reanalyze; neither states that an unavailable result counts as a populated cache. The doc is silent on cache validity, so this is a gap rather than a divergence.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: Re-uploading a map image does not invalidate image_segments, so a default analyze returns the previous image's segments
findings.what_code_does: _handle_upload_map_image's success block (926-958) writes the PNG, records/overwrites `image_variants[variant]`, optionally repoints a layout's backdrop/art variant, and saves. It never touches `image_segments`, `image_segment_adjustments`, or `segment_room_links`, and it stamps no marker that the analyzed image has changed. _handle_analyze_map_image's cache gate (1100) therefore still reports a hit for a segmentation computed from the REPLACED image, with the old `analyzed_at` and the old `image` dims.
findings.reproduction: Call upload_map_image(map_id="5", variant="dark", image_base64=<new 1200x800 export>) — the file at eufy_vacuum/maps/<obj>/map_5_dark.png is overwritten and image_variants["dark"] now says 1200x800. Then call analyze_map_image(map_id="5") with no force_reanalyze (schema default False). Line 1100 returns the cached store from the OLD 600x400 image; get_map_segments then divides those polygons by the OLD store dims (1224-1226) and hands the card polygon_pct values describing rooms in an image that no longer exists on disk.
findings.user_impact: An automation or script that uploads a refreshed map export and analyzes it gets the previous map's room geometry back with a success-shaped response and no staleness signal. The card path is immune (it always passes force_reanalyze:true), so this is an edge case confined to service callers — but the invalidation belongs on the write side, and its absence is exactly why the card had to hard-code the flag.
findings.guards_checked: (a) the `if result["saved"]` block at 926 — updates only image_variants and layout pointers; (b) `analyzed_at` at 1173 — stamped only on a real run, so the stale response carries the old timestamp (detectable, but only by a caller that knows to compare); (c) _variant_path at 1109 — re-resolves the file path on a real run but is never reached on a cache hit; (d) no mtime/size/hash comparison between the stored envelope and the file.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 / §6.1 describe upload_map_image as writing the PNG and recording variant metadata; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:604-620 (§3b) lists exactly the same effects. Neither doc claims upload invalidates the segmentation cache, and neither warns that it does not — the coupling is simply undocumented in both directions.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: Image filenames are built from an unsanitised free-form map_id, so one map's upload can silently overwrite another map's image
findings.what_code_does: `suffix = "" if variant == "default" else f"_{variant}"` then `file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")` (895-896), with `browser_url` built the same way (897) and _handle_delete_map_image reproducing the identical construction at 999-1000. `map_id` is `cv.string` — free-form, and on Roborock it is the map NAME reported verbatim by the active-map entity, so spaces and underscores are normal. The map_id and the variant are concatenated into one flat filename with an underscore separator and no escaping, quoting, length cap, or character filter. Storage keys stay distinct (ensure_map_bucket uses str(map_id) as a dict key), which is precisely why the collision is silent — the two buckets disagree with the filesystem, not with each other.
findings.reproduction: Arithmetic on the name construction. Map A has map_id "Upstairs"; map B has map_id "Upstairs_dark" (a legal Roborock map name). upload_map_image(map_id="Upstairs", variant="dark") -> "map_Upstairs_dark.png". upload_map_image(map_id="Upstairs_dark", variant="default") -> "map_Upstairs_dark.png". Same path: the second upload overwrites the first map's dark segmenter input, and both buckets' image_variants records now advertise the same file with different recorded dims. delete_map_image(map_id="Upstairs", variant="dark") then removes map B's default backdrop while map B's bucket still lists it — after which analyze for map B either reports image_not_found or (if another variant exists) segments a different image than the one recorded. Second, cheaper failure: map_id "Main/2nd" makes file_path ".../map_Main/2nd.png", whose parent directory was never created (only base_dir is, line 900), so open(...,"wb") raises FileNotFoundError inside the executor and propagates out of the service — every other failure in this handler returns a structured {"saved": False, "reason": ...}, so the caller gets a traceback instead of a reason. On a POSIX host a map_id beginning "../" resolves outside base_dir entirely (components [.., maps, <obj>, "map_..", "..", "x.png"] collapse to .../maps/x.png), so the PNG lands outside the intended directory and delete_map_image will later os.remove that stored path.
findings.user_impact: The user edits/uploads a backdrop for the map they named and it lands on a different map's file, with the storage records still claiming otherwise — a direct answer to 'does the edit land on the map it names?' being 'not guaranteed'. Requires an unfortunate but legal map name (a name ending in _dark/_light/_custom, or containing a path separator), so the common numeric-map_id Eufy path is unaffected; Roborock's name-as-map_id makes it reachable without any malicious intent.
findings.guards_checked: (a) _image_variant (313-318) — constrains the VARIANT half of the filename only; there is no equivalent validator for map_id; (b) cv.string on map_id in all five schemas — type check only, no charset/normalisation; (c) ensure_map_bucket's str(map_id) keying — keeps STORAGE distinct, which is what makes the filesystem collision invisible; (d) os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True) at 900 — creates only the base dir, so a separator in map_id is a hard failure not a nested write; (e) no os.path.commonpath / basename / slugify anywhere in the module.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6.1 documents the path template `map_<map_id>[_<variant>].png` and explicitly claims "Variant names are normalised to lowercase, spaces and hyphens replaced by underscores" (line 517). No normalisation exists anywhere in the code — not for variants (the whitelist masks it) and not for map_id or the derived art keys `custom_<id>_room_<room_id>`, where a room id containing a space would produce a filename and a browser_url with a raw space. The doc's own examples assume a numeric map_id (map_6_dark.png).
findings.brands_affected: Both; Roborock materially more exposed because get_active_map_id returns the user-authored map NAME verbatim.

findings.title: delete_map_image calls itself the mirror of upload but has no layout_id/art_scope sibling and sweeps no back-references
findings.what_code_does: The docstring at 965-974 calls this handler a "Mirror of _handle_upload_map_image". It is not. Upload is layout-aware in three ways: it accepts layout_id, derives the variant key (`custom_<layout_id>`, `custom_<id>_home_art`, `custom_<id>_room_<rid>`), verifies the layout exists before writing, and repoints `layout["backdrop_variant"]` / `layout["home_art"]["art_variant"]` / `layout["rooms"][rid]["art_variant"]` (846-875, 941-957). Delete accepts only (vacuum_entity_id, map_id, variant) — DELETE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:339-345 has no layout_id and no art_scope — and its whole mutation is `variants.pop(variant, None)` at 1014. No layout, art record, or `image_segments` reference to the removed variant is inspected or cleared. The reverse direction was implemented: _handle_delete_custom_layout (2392-2418) deliberately sweeps the layout's backdrop and art variants out of image_variants and off disk. Only this half of the pair is missing — the campaign's forgotten-override-sibling shape, with a permissive default (variant defaults to "default") making the omission silent.
findings.reproduction: Create custom layout cl_A and upload its backdrop: upload_map_image(map_id="5", layout_id="cl_A", variant="custom") -> variant forced to "custom_cl_A", image_variants["custom_cl_A"] = {width: 1024, height: 768, ...}, layout.backdrop_variant = "custom_cl_A". Author segments against it. Now call delete_map_image(map_id="5", variant="custom_cl_A") — _image_variant accepts any custom_* key, so the schema permits it. Result: the PNG is gone and image_variants no longer has the key, but layout.backdrop_variant still reads "custom_cl_A". Next set_custom_segments for that layout does `backdrop = image_variants.get("custom_cl_A") or {}` -> `map_w = None` -> returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"} (1669-1684) for a layout that still exists, still renders its previously authored polygons, and reports a backdrop_variant in the get_map_segments layouts_summary (1256). Same for home_art.art_variant / rooms[rid].art_variant, which no cleanup path other than layout deletion ever revisits.
findings.user_impact: A layout survives its backdrop and becomes uneditable with a misleading reason ('no custom backdrop') while continuing to advertise one; get_map_segments silently substitutes the CV dark/default/light image metadata for the missing backdrop (1211-1217), so the layout's authored geometry is composed over a different picture than it was drawn on. Reachable only by a direct service call today (the card's variant list is dark/light/default only — src/renderers/map.js:76-80), which is why it rates MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the same asymmetry also means a per-layout backdrop or furnished-art PNG can never be removed through the card at all.
findings.guards_checked: (a) `if not isinstance(entry, dict)` at 988 — only checks that the variant is recorded, never who references it; (b) _image_variant at 316 — actively ADMITS custom_* keys into the delete path, so the schema is not the guard; (c) the two-tap arm/confirm in the card (src/bindings/map.js:1129-1150) — a UI confirmation for the three CV variants only, absent for any service caller; (d) _handle_delete_custom_layout:2392-2418 — proves the reference sweep exists in the codebase, in the other direction only; (e) no reference count, no reverse index from variant -> layout.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510-511 documents that upload with layout_id/art_scope repoints backdrop_variant / home_art.art_variant / rooms[<rid>].art_variant; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:619-626 (§3b, 'Per-layout upload') documents the same repointing. Neither doc describes any delete-side counterpart. docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:358 states image_variants is "Written by upload_map_image, pruned by delete_map_image" — pruning the variant map is exactly all it does, so the doc is accurate about the mechanism and silent about the dangling reference it creates.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: delete_map_image drops the storage record and reports deleted:True even when the file removal failed, and analyze's filesystem probe then re-uses the orphan
findings.what_code_does: _remove_file (1002-1010) returns False on OSError after a warning log, and returns False on FileNotFoundError. The caller ignores the distinction: lines 1014-1022 pop the variant and save unconditionally, and the result at 1024-1031 reports `deleted: True` with the real outcome demoted to a secondary `file_removed` field. The card's caller checks only `result.deleted !== false` (src/bindings/map.js:1157-1161) and shows a success toast, so the failure is discarded end to end — the codebase's documented 'result-returning APIs whose failure is discarded' pattern. The orphaned PNG is then still live to the analyzer: _variant_path (1109-1113) falls back to `os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")` whenever the variant is absent from image_variants, and 1118-1123 accepts it on `os.path.isfile`.
findings.reproduction: delete_map_image(map_id="5", variant="dark") while map_5_dark.png cannot be unlinked (open handle / permission / read-only mount) -> os.remove raises PermissionError (an OSError) -> _remove_file returns False -> line 1014 still pops image_variants["dark"] and line 1022 persists. The card refetches segments, the IMAGE VARIANTS row for dark now renders 'not uploaded', and the user is toasted 'deleted'. The user then presses Analyse: _variant_path("dark") finds no variant record, rebuilds the conventional path, os.path.isfile returns True, and the segmenter re-analyzes the very image the user believed they deleted, stamping image_variant "dark" into the tuning and a fresh analyzed_at.
findings.user_impact: The user is told a bad upload was removed, the UI agrees it is gone, and the segmenter keeps using it — the delete is neither honest nor effective. Also leaves an undeletable orphan: with no image_variants record, a second delete_map_image returns {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} at 989 and never retries the unlink, so nothing in the integration can ever remove that file again. Requires the unlink to actually fail, which is uncommon on the usual Linux host, hence MEDIUM.
findings.guards_checked: (a) `except FileNotFoundError: return False` at 1006 — deliberately makes the handler idempotent, and the docstring's 'safe to call multiple times' claim only covers that branch, not the OSError branch; (b) the `except OSError` warning log at 1008-1009 — logs and swallows; (c) the `file_removed` field in the response — present, and ignored by the only caller; (d) `remaining_variants` at 1030 — reports what the storage now says, not what is on disk; (e) analyze's `os.path.isfile` at 1120 — treats the filesystem as authoritative, which is the opposite of what the delete path assumed.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:358 says image_variants is "pruned by delete_map_image" — accurate for the storage half, silent on the file half. The handler docstring (965-975) states it "removes the PNG ... and drops the variant" and is "safe to call multiple times"; per rule 2 that is a claim, and the OSError branch falsifies the first half while leaving the second half (the storage pop) executed anyway. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6.1 documents that the analyzer resolves images by the conventional path, confirming the orphan is reachable.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: min_area_pixels silently overrides the adapter's configured tuning because absent is coerced to 1200 before the is-not-None check
findings.what_code_does: The handler layers caller kwargs over the adapter's persisted `segmenter_tuning` (1147-1161). Three of the four knobs do this correctly: expected_room_count, max_segments and simplify_epsilon are read with a bare `call.data.get(...)` (1087-1090) and only written into `tuning` when not None, so an omitted field leaves the adapter's value standing. The fourth does not: `min_area_pixels: int = call.data.get("min_area_pixels", 1200)` at 1089 substitutes the literal 1200 for 'absent', after which `if min_area_pixels is not None` at 1152 is always true and `tuning["min_area_pixels"] = 1200` unconditionally clobbers whatever the adapter declared. ANALYZE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:353 deliberately gives this field NO voluptuous default (unlike the legacy GET_IMAGE_SEGMENT_SUGGESTIONS_SCHEMA:212, which does), so absence is representable at the schema layer and is discarded one line later. 1200 is also a hand-copied literal living in four places — here, segmenter_engines.py:273, adapters/eufy/adapter.py:600, and docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1099.
findings.reproduction: Adapter config declares mapping.segmenter_tuning = {"min_area_pixels": 400} (a documented knob for maps with small rooms). Call analyze_map_image(vacuum_entity_id=..., map_id="5") with no min_area_pixels. Line 1147 seeds tuning = {"min_area_pixels": 400}; line 1153 overwrites it with 1200; the engine receives 1200 (segmenter_engines.py:273) and every component between 400 and 1199 px is dropped as a tiny region. The adapter's configured value is unreachable from any caller that does not restate it, and no warning is logged.
findings.user_impact: An adapter-level segmentation tuning knob that the adapter-config reference documents as configurable is silently inert for the omit-the-field case, so small rooms vanish from the segmentation with no diagnostic. Masked today because the only shipped adapter declares exactly 1200 — the bug is invisible until someone tunes it, which is precisely the forgotten-sibling shape (three knobs wired correctly, the fourth not, with a permissive default hiding it).
findings.guards_checked: (a) `if min_area_pixels is not None` at 1152 — cannot fire, the .get default already removed the None; (b) EufyCVSegmenter.validate_tuning (segmenter_engines.py:218-226) — validates the value's type/range at registration, never that it survived to the engine; (c) segmenter_engines.py:273 `int(tuning.get("min_area_pixels", 1200))` — its own fallback would have handled the absent case correctly had the handler not injected one; (d) the sibling knobs at 1148/1150/1154 — inspected and correct, which is what isolates this line.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1085-1125 documents segmenter_tuning as engine-owned knobs and states that _handle_analyze_map_image "layers caller kwargs over the adapter's segmenter_tuning" — min_area_pixels is not a caller kwarg here, so injecting it diverges from the documented precedence. The handler's own comment at 1136-1138 ("Tuning starts from the adapter's persisted defaults; call.data fields override them") makes the same claim and is falsified by the next 20 lines.
findings.brands_affected: Both; any adapter that tunes min_area_pixels away from 1200.

findings.title: Upload persists width/height as None when Pillow is unavailable and still reports saved:True
findings.what_code_does: _write_and_measure (899-922) measures the written PNG with Pillow and, on any exception (including ImportError), falls back to `declared_width`/`declared_height` from call.data. Those are Optional with no default (UPLOAD_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:328-329) and the card never sends them — src/actions/map.js:231-243 forwards only {variant, layout_id, art_scope}. So with Pillow absent the record written at 934-940 is {"width": None, "height": None} and the handler still returns saved:True with no reason field. Pillow is an optional dependency by design here (manifest requirements are empty; segment_primitives.image_runtime_capabilities exists precisely to probe it).
findings.reproduction: HA instance without Pillow. Upload a PNG backdrop for a custom layout: the bytes already start with the PNG magic so the conversion branch at 882-891 is skipped and the write succeeds; PIL.Image import fails at 906 so actual_width/height fall back to the absent declared values -> image_variants["custom_cl_A"] = {width: None, height: None}. set_custom_segments then evaluates `if not map_w or not map_h` (1673) as true for a backdrop that was uploaded successfully and, unless the caller separately supplies backdrop_width/height (src/actions/map.js:475 sends them only when the caller passes measured dims), returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"}. The card's variant row also renders the raw values as "null × null" (src/renderers/map.js:1770).
findings.user_impact: On a Pillow-less install a successful upload is recorded in a state that makes custom-segment authoring report a missing backdrop, and the variant row displays null dimensions. Confined to installs without Pillow, and the recorded dims are the only casualty (the PNG itself is correct), hence LOW.
findings.guards_checked: (a) the try/except at 905-911 — deliberately degrades to declared dims, but nothing checks that declared dims exist; (b) the schema's Optional image_width/image_height — no defaults, no requirement that at least one source of dims be present; (c) `if result["saved"]` at 926 — saved is hard-coded True in _write_and_measure and never reflects the measurement outcome; (d) set_custom_segments' `no_custom_backdrop` return (1684) — catches it downstream with a reason that names the wrong cause.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510 states the recorded image_width/image_height "define the pixel space set_custom_segments rasterises that layout's authored polygons against"; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:604-618 (§3b) describes the VariantRecord as carrying width/height. Neither doc contemplates a record with null dims, and §2.11 documents Pillow as an optional, probed dependency — so the two statements are in tension.
findings.brands_affected: Both; depends on whether Pillow is importable on the host.

findings.title: Layout existence is validated before the executor write and re-checked afterwards only by a silent isinstance guard, so a concurrent layout delete orphans the upload
findings.what_code_does: For the layout-scoped branches the handler validates the layout at 863/874 (returning layout_not_found), then awaits the executor file write at 924 — a real suspension point in the single event loop, and a slow one for a multi-megabyte PNG. After resuming it re-fetches the layout at 945/954 and guards with `if isinstance(layout, dict)`, which silently skips the repointing when the layout has since disappeared. The file has already been written and image_variants[variant] is recorded unconditionally at 933-940, and the handler still returns saved:True with no indication that the layout link was not made.
findings.reproduction: upload_map_image(map_id="5", layout_id="cl_A", art_scope="home") begins; while the executor writes the PNG, delete_custom_layout(layout_id="cl_A") runs on the loop and pops the layout plus its known art variants (2412-2420) — it cannot know about the art variant still in flight. The upload resumes: `layout` is None, the isinstance guard skips, image_variants["custom_cl_A_home_art"] is written and saved, and the PNG stays on disk. Result: a variant record and file referencing a layout that no longer exists, with the service reporting success. Nothing can clean it up — delete_custom_layout for cl_A already ran, and the card's delete UI covers only dark/light/default (IMAGE--6).
findings.user_impact: A leaked PNG plus a phantom image_variants entry, and an upload the user believes attached to their layout that attached to nothing. Requires two service calls to overlap across a single await, so it is rare in practice; the missing part is that the post-await re-check has no failure reason and the earlier validation is never re-honoured.
findings.guards_checked: (a) the pre-write layout_not_found checks at 849-875 — validated before the await, and the code correctly does not trust them afterwards; (b) `if isinstance(layout, dict)` at 946/955 — the re-check exists but its else branch is silence rather than a reason or a rollback of the just-written file; (c) delete_custom_layout's variant sweep (2392-2418) — runs before the in-flight variant is recorded, so it cannot cover it; (d) HA's single event loop — the interleaving here is genuinely across an await (async_add_executor_job), not two coroutines inside a synchronous block, so this is not a same-block false positive.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md:619-626 (§3b, 'Per-layout upload') documents the sequence as validate -> write PNG -> repoint backdrop_variant, i.e. the validation is described as governing the whole operation. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510-511 describes the same contract. Neither doc addresses concurrency, so this is a gap rather than a divergence.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

findings.title: Four of the five services in this block have no services.yaml description, including the destructive delete_map_image
findings.what_code_does: All five handlers are registered with schemas and supports_response=True (2814-2833), but services.yaml declares only set_segmentation_mode (line 2419). upload_map_image, delete_map_image, analyze_map_image, get_map_segments and adjust_map_segment have no top-level entry at all, while their siblings registered in the same block (set_segment_room_link:2385, set_segmentation_mode:2419, set_custom_segments:2449, the whole saved-zone family:2773-2923) do. Verified by exact-key grep over services.yaml.
findings.reproduction: Open Developer Tools -> Actions in HA and search for eufy_vacuum.delete_map_image: the action appears (registration succeeds without a description) but with no name, no description, and no field editors, so calling it requires hand-writing the YAML payload including the exact variant key. Same for upload_map_image, analyze_map_image and get_map_segments.
findings.user_impact: No runtime behaviour change — this is documentation/UI surface only. The consequence is that the one destructive service in this area (delete_map_image, which removes a file from disk) is the least discoverable and least documented, and neither its two-tap card guard nor any field description reaches a user driving it from Developer Tools or an automation. Also a quality-scale gap (HA expects every registered service to have a description).
findings.guards_checked: (a) hass.services.async_register at 2814-2833 — registers successfully with or without a description, so nothing fails loudly; (b) ALL_MAPPING_SERVICES (73-109) — lists every service name for registration/teardown but is not tied to services.yaml, so there is no cross-check; (c) the card calls these by constant (src/constants.js:120-122), so the missing descriptions never surface in the UI path that is actually exercised.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §7 line 543 shows the project does track services.yaml presence when it matters (it explicitly records the retired bounds services as "absent from services.yaml"). No dev doc claims services.yaml completeness for the mapping block, so this is an unstated gap rather than a contradicted claim.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

clean_areas: _build_segments_response (1036-1081) — the docstring's central claim, 'The original image_segments cache is NOT mutated', VERIFIED: `response = dict(base)` shallow-copies the envelope, the per-segment enrichment builds `seg = {**seg, "room_id": ...}` into a fresh `enriched` list rather than mutating the cached dicts, and `companion_anchors` is copied with dict(). The non-dict early return at 1056-1057 and the isinstance coercions of links/anchors at 1060-1063 are correct defensive reads. No setdefault, no write-back — a genuinely pure read path, unusual for this codebase.

_handle_set_segmentation_mode (1319-1350) — the stated INVARIANT holds exactly. The handler writes only `segmentation_mode`, plus a soft-select of `sorted(layouts)[0]` when flipping to custom with no active layout; it never calls get_segmenter_engine, never touches image_segments or any layout's custom_segments, and the final `_resolve_active_scope(...)` read at 1348 is only used to count segments for the response. cv -> custom -> cv is genuinely lossless. Matches docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md line 766 and docs/dev/03-data-model.md §3a.

_handle_get_map_segments pixel->pct divisor (1218-1233) — the store-dims-over-variant-dims preference is correct and matches docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §2.10 line 202 exactly, including the reason (a live-image-backed custom layout has no uploaded image_variant, so the variant chain would leave the divisor at 1). The `isinstance(raw.get("image"), dict)` narrowing at 1224 is right, and the `or` chain at 1225-1226 cannot eat a legitimate 0 because a zero-width image is not a meaningful state.

analyze_map_image tuning override precedence for the three non-defaulted knobs (1087-1161) — expected_room_count, max_segments and simplify_epsilon are read with a bare .get() and guarded by `is not None`, so an omitted field correctly leaves the adapter's persisted value standing, and an explicit simplify_epsilon of 0.0 is NOT eaten by an `or` (the classic falsy-coercion trap is avoided here). Only min_area_pixels breaks the pattern — reported as IMAGE--11.

analyze_map_image image selection (1104-1134) — the dark-then-default primary probe with light as an optional assist matches docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 ("the segmenter reads dark/default/light exclusively and never reads any custom* variant"). The variant-record-then-filesystem-probe fallback in _variant_path (1109-1113) is a sensible resolution order, `variants[v].get("path")` is truthiness-checked before use, and the image_not_found early return at 1125-1131 fires before any bucket mutation.

upload_map_image input decoding and format normalisation (877-891) — base64 decode failure and non-PNG conversion failure both return structured {"saved": False, "reason": ...} rather than raising, the PNG magic check is a byte-prefix test (not an extension sniff), and the Pillow re-encode is correctly scoped to the non-PNG case so a valid PNG is never re-compressed. The furnished-art validation ladder at 846-864 (layout_id required, room_id required and stripped for scope=room, layout must already exist) correctly validates BEFORE any file is written, and derives the variant key rather than trusting the caller's.

upload_map_image art/backdrop write separation (941-957) — furnished art writes only home_art.art_variant / rooms[rid].art_variant and deliberately does NOT touch backdrop_variant, while the layout-backdrop branch writes only backdrop_variant; both bump updated_at. This matches docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 511 and docs/dev/03-data-model.md §3b precisely — the two variant families cannot cross-contaminate.

_apply_segment_adjustments / _adjust_polygon_pixel arithmetic (695-825) — the geometry itself is sound: the 10%-band edge test uses the pre-translation min/max so edge nudges are computed against the original bbox, vertex moves are range-checked (idx < 0 or idx >= len), the bbox and center_pixel are recomputed from the adjusted polygon rather than nudged independently, and the no-op fast paths at 761-762 and 782-784 avoid stamping *_manual issue tags on unadjusted segments. The defect is in WHICH segment the adjustment is matched to (IMAGE--1), not in the transform.

_handle_get_map_segments overlay scoping (1235-1316) — hidden_regions and area_label_anchors are correctly served from the map bucket (mode-independent physical masks / device rooms) while links and anchors come from _resolve_active_scope, and both are isinstance-guarded before being copied out. The layouts_summary whitelist at 1252-1269 does include the furnished keys (render_mode, home_art, rooms) that the comment says are otherwise unreachable by the editor.

delete_map_image idempotency for the never-uploaded case (986-995) — returning {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} with the echoed identifiers, before any filesystem work, is the right shape; the `not isinstance(entry, dict)` test correctly rejects a corrupt non-dict variant record as well as a missing one.
not_examined: adapters/eufy/segmentor.py internals — deliberately excluded by the brief. I read only the segment_id assignment sites (1085, 1289, 1394, 1414, 1474, 1485) to establish that segment ids are positional/area-ranked, which IMAGE--1 depends on; I made no judgement on the CV algorithm itself.

mapping/segmenter_engines.py — owned by another reviewer. I read segment_map_image (249-293), _reshape (299-326), get_segmenter_engine (385-403) and _engine_unavailable (416-440) purely to establish the failure-envelope contract that IMAGE--2 and IMAGE--3 turn on. No findings filed against that file.
mapping/map_source.py, map_source_runtime.py, map_source_coordinator.py, tracker.py — out of scope (audit #11).
mapping/segment_primitives.py and roborock_raw_map.py — not in my line range; rasterize_primitives and polygon_area were treated as black boxes.

mapping_services.py outside 828-1352 — I read _apply_segment_adjustments/_adjust_polygon_pixel (695-825), the schemas (115-442), _migrate_custom_layouts/_resolve_active_scope/_create_layout/_build_custom_segment (1474-1642), _handle_set_custom_segments (1644-1730), _handle_adjust_map_segment (1733-1803), _handle_delete_custom_layout (2374-2441) and the registration block (2715-2834) only as context for my handlers. Findings are anchored in my range; no independent audit of those regions was performed.

The saved-zone family (_migrate_saved_zones, _backfill_saved_zone_area, the CRUD at 2475-2710) — _handle_get_map_segments calls the migration and the backfill (1273-1279), and I note that this makes a read path write and persist, but the backfill's own correctness belongs to another reviewer.

Runtime verification — nothing was executed. No HA instance, no test run, no filesystem experiment; every claim is traced from source, with the two runtime-dependent items flagged as needs-runtime-check.
Card-side rendering beyond the specific call sites cited (src/actions/map.js, src/bindings/map.js, src/renderers/map.js) — inspected only to establish reachability and what the user sees.

findings.title: A raster containing ZERO rooms is published as present:True — decode's own room_ids signal is computed and discarded
findings.what_code_does: decode_roborock_v1_segments computes `room_ids = sorted(b for b in set(room_pixels) if 1 <= b <= MAX_ROOM_RID)` (line 116) — the one signal that says whether the decoded segment layer actually contains any rooms. roborock_render_data never reads it. Its only emptiness gate is `if not rp or not width or not height: return None` (line 158), and `rp` is an all-zero bytes object, which is truthy. So a raster with no room pixels at all is wrapped as `{present: True, ...}` with no `reason`, and `roborock_render_data_from_candidates` (map_source_runtime.py:411, `if rd is not None: return rd`) stops scanning further candidate roots because it got a non-None answer.
findings.reproduction: Blob = 20-byte map header (map_header_len @0x02 = 20) + one IMAGE block (type 2, header_len 24, data_len 30000, top 0, left 0, height 150, width 200) + 30000 bytes of 0x07 (MAP_SCAN — the state of every pixel while the robot is part-way through its FIRST mapping run, or after a map reset). Executed against the shipped module: `decode_roborock_v1_segments(blob)` returns room_ids=[] with 0 non-zero pixels (resolve_rid(0x07)==0), and `roborock_render_data(dec, {16: 'Kitchen'})` returns `present=True, width=200, height=150, room_names={'16': 'Kitchen'}`. Expected: an absent marker so the caller falls through to `{present: False, reason: 'no_raw_map'}`.
findings.user_impact: The card's `isVaRenderActive()` (src/state/map.js:1201) only tests `mapRenderData()?.present`, so the VA (▦) backdrop switches on over a completely blank canvas, replacing the live Roborock map image the user was looking at. Every pixel hit-test (`roomIdAtContentPct`, src/state/map.js:965) returns null because rid is 0 everywhere, so the auto-derived click targets vanish and rooms become unclickable; per-room colours and floor textures disappear with them. Nothing surfaces a reason — the card, and diagnostics' self_check 'map decoded' verdict, both read this as a successfully decoded map. Common path (a fully mapped device) is unaffected; this bites during a first/partial scan, after a map reset, or if the BFS locks onto a stale MapContent.
findings.guards_checked: roborock_render_data:158 `if not rp or not width or not height` — rp is b'\x00'*30000, truthy, passes. decode_roborock_v1_segments:111-114 (`width<=0 or height<=0 or pixel_count>data_len`, `data_start+pixel_count>n`) — all satisfied by a well-formed but unassigned blob. decode's own room_ids (line 116-118) — computed, never consulted by any caller. map_source_runtime.py:411 `if rd is not None` — accepts. map_source_coordinator.py:622-630 format dispatch — no post-check on the returned payload. src/bindings/map.js:223 `if (!canvas || !rd || !rd.present) return` — present is True.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §`map_render` (states the raster's purpose is per-room colour / floor textures / pixel-exact hit-test — an all-background raster delivers none of them, and the doc never contemplates one). docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4, which states the contract as 'Degrades to {present: False, reason}'.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

findings.title: raster_room_bboxes runs an O(width*height) pure-Python per-pixel loop directly on the Home Assistant event loop
findings.what_code_does: `for i, rid in enumerate(rp)` at line 200 iterates EVERY pixel of the decoded raster in Python, doing `i % w`, `i // w`, a dict `.get`, and up to four comparisons per pixel. There is no size cap: decode_roborock_v1_segments bounds width/height only by the blob length (lines 111-114), so the loop length is whatever the device's IMAGE block is.
