The call chain is entirely synchronous: raster_room_bboxes ← geometry_drift (line 259) ← map_source_runtime.roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates:434 ← diagnostics.py:503, which sits inside `_vacuum_diagnostics(...)` — a plain sync function invoked from the coroutine `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` at diagnostics.py:571, in a list comprehension, once per vacuum, with no `async_add_executor_job`.
findings.reproduction: Roborock S6, map_state_source.backend == 'memory', a decodable raw blob. Settings → Devices & Services → Vacuum Agent → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. For an IMAGE block of 700x700 (a routine crop for a whole-floor S6 map) that is 490,000 Python loop iterations with two integer divisions and a dict lookup each, executed on the event loop thread. Contrast the render path for the SAME raster: decode_roborock_v1_segments + roborock_render_data touch every pixel only through `bytes.translate`, `set()`, `base64.b64encode` and `hashlib.sha1` — all C-level. The drift path is the only per-pixel Python loop in the module, and it is the one that is not offloaded.
findings.user_impact: Downloading diagnostics stalls the entire HA event loop — every integration, every automation trigger, the frontend websocket — for the duration of the scan. On x86 that is roughly 0.1-0.3 s for a mid-size map; on a Pi-class or NAS host with a large map it is comfortably into multiple seconds, long enough for HA's own loop-lag warnings and for a websocket-connected card to visibly freeze. It repeats once per configured Roborock vacuum in the same download. Not data loss, and only on a user-initiated diagnostics download — but it is the one path in this module with no cost bound at all.
findings.guards_checked: diagnostics.py:496-505 — a bare try/except around the call, no executor hop, no size or timeout guard. diagnostics.py:533-574 — `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` is a coroutine and calls `_vacuum_diagnostics` synchronously at :571. map_source_coordinator.py:620 comments 'In-memory + pure -> loop-safe' — that claim covers the RENDER path (roborock_render_data_from_candidates), which is genuinely C-level; it does not cover the drift path, and the drift path has no equivalent claim or guard. decode_roborock_v1_segments has no maximum-dimension check that would bound the loop. geometry_drift/raster_room_bboxes have no early-exit or sampling.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §'Surfaced in diagnostics' — 'This drift-check runs automatically ... best-effort, never raises.' The doc's only stated non-functional property is 'never raises'; nothing is claimed or reasoned about loop cost. docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4 explicitly reasons about loop-safety for the render reader but says nothing about the drift validator.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

findings.title: `version` hashes the raster ONLY, while the payload also ships room_names — a room rename cannot invalidate a fetched render payload
findings.what_code_does: Line 163: `version = hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()[:12]` where `raw = bytes(rp)` is the room-id raster and nothing else. The payload returned two lines later also carries `room_names` (line 178), sourced live from managed rooms via map_source_coordinator._roborock_render_room_names. So the declared content hash covers one half of the payload's content and silently omits the half that changes when the user edits the map. There is no other identity in the payload either — no map_id, no room-set stamp.
findings.reproduction: Roborock, VA (▦) render active, room segment 16 named 'Kitchen' with a per-room colour override and a floor type set. (1) Card fetches render data once: room_names={'16':'Kitchen'}, version=sha1(raster). (2) User renames the room to 'Cocina' in the card. The raster bytes are untouched (a rename does not re-map the device), so any recomputed version would be byte-identical — and the card does not refetch on version change anyway: src/bindings/map.js:199 refetches only `if (!rd ...)`, and src/bindings/map.js:195 clears rd only when `activeMapId` changes. (3) src/bindings/map.js:335-346 bridges raster rid → the user's room BY NAME: `rgbByName` is built from the CURRENT rooms ('cocina') and looked up with `norm(ridNames[ridStr])` = 'kitchen'. Lookup misses, `overrideByRid[16]` stays unset.
findings.user_impact: Immediately after renaming a room, that room's custom fill colour and its floor-type material silently disappear from the rendered map and it reverts to the default palette fill — with no error and no way to tell why. It stays wrong until the user reloads the card or switches the active map. The card's own comment (src/bindings/map.js:326-330) states that the name bridge is the ONLY correct bridge ('Keying by room.id directly is WRONG — the raster rid and our stored room.id are DIFFERENT id spaces on real devices'), so there is no fallback path. This is squarely the 'does the edit survive?' question: the edit lands in storage but the map render keeps rendering against the pre-edit vocabulary. Note the Eufy sibling map_source.eufy_version_of:621-628 has the identical raster-only hash, so this is a shared contract, not a Roborock-only slip — but Roborock's is the one minted here.
findings.guards_checked: roborock_render_data:162-163 — `version` is only auto-computed when the caller passes None; no caller passes anything, so the raster-only hash always wins. No room_names, map_id, or room-set contribution to the hash. src/bindings/map.js:190-201 — the only invalidation is `_renderDataMapId !== mapId`; a rename does not change map_id. src/state/map.js:1192-1197 — setMapRenderData/mapRenderVersion just store and read; nothing compares versions to decide a refetch. src/bindings/map.js:355-356 — the ImageData cache keys on `rd.version` AND `overrideSig`, but overrideSig is itself derived from the stale ridNames, so the cache is self-consistently stale rather than incoherent.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4: 'The card calls this on demand ... and caches by the returned `version`; the raster is static (changes only on a re-map), so it's fetch-once'. The doc asserts the payload is static, which is true of the raster but false of room_names — the doc calmly documents the fetch-once policy without reconciling it against the mutable field in the same payload. docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render describes room_names as coming from 'the adapter's discovered rooms' with no freshness contract.
findings.brands_affected: roborock (the identical raster-only version hash exists for eufy in map_source.eufy_version_of, out of scope here)

findings.title: ro_dx/ro_dy are hardcoded 0 and the decoded top/left are discarded — the payload cannot express any offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame
findings.what_code_does: decode_roborock_v1_segments reads `top` and `left` from the IMAGE-block header (lines 97-98) and returns them (lines 122-123), and then no consumer in the module ever uses them: roborock_render_data ignores them and instead hardcodes `ro_dx: 0, ro_dy: 0` (lines 171-172) with `ro_width/ro_height` set equal to the canvas (lines 169-170), defended by the comment 'the raster IS the canvas (no outline frame)'. That comment is a CLAIM that the raw IMAGE-block frame is pixel-identical to the frame every other Roborock overlay is normalized to — namely map_source_runtime._mapdata_projector (:438-470), which normalizes by the PARSER's rendered `image.data.size` after `dims.to_img` has applied the parser's trim/scale. The ro_dx/ro_dy fields exist precisely to carry such an offset (Eufy fills them from _outline_geometry, map_source.py:662-663); Roborock is the sibling where the knob is present but pinned to 0.
findings.reproduction: Conditional on the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim, which is not inspectable from this repo. If the parser trims T rows off the rendered image's bottom of an H-row block: raw row r normalizes to (H-1-r)/H in this module's frame (raster_room_bboxes:219) but to (H-T-1-r)/(H-T) in the parser frame. H=700, T=50, r=100 → 0.8557 vs 0.8446, a 0.011 normalized delta = 0.39 m on a 700 px x 50 mm/px (35 m) map. If T==0 the frames coincide and this is inert. The shipped geometry_drift diagnostic is exactly the instrument that settles it: one 'Download diagnostics' on the real S6 reports `aligned` (frames coincide, no defect) or a systematic `max_center_delta` (frames differ, defect live).
findings.user_impact: IF the frames differ: the card draws the raster full-bleed at 0..1 while every overlay it composites on top — room bboxes, robot/dock anchors, no-go and no-mop quads, saved zones — comes from map_state_source in the parser frame, so overlays sit offset from the rooms they label; `roomIdAtContentPct` (src/state/map.js:931-966) names the wrong room for clicks near a boundary; and a zone drawn on the raster is converted to device mm through `correspondences_from_mapdata` (the PARSER frame) at dispatch/manager.py:154, so app_zoned_clean cleans a displaced rectangle — the robot physically cleans the wrong strip of floor. The round-trip refuse-gate cannot catch it: zone_dispatch.max_residual_mm validates the affine against parser-frame correspondences only, which are self-consistent, so the residual is ~0 and the dispatch proceeds. Discarding top/left removes the only data in the blob that could have detected or corrected the offset.
findings.guards_checked: roborock_render_data:169-172 — ro_* hardcoded, no derivation from decoded top/left. decode_roborock_v1_segments:122-123 — top/left returned but consumed by nothing in the module or its callers (grepped). zone_dispatch.normalized_rects_to_mm:119 round-trip gate — validates the fit against the same parser-frame points it was fit from, so a frame MISMATCH between card and dispatch is invisible to it. src/state/map.js:940-942 letterbox aspect — falls back to rd.width/height when image_size is absent, with the comment 'Both derive from the same md.width/height, so this is byte-identical whenever both exist', which is true for Eufy but is the same unverified claim for Roborock. geometry_drift exists and would detect it, but it is diagnostics-only and its verdict gates nothing.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §Drift-check states outright that a delta is expected and that 'a constant offset = the parser's trim' — i.e. the doc anticipates the frames differing, yet the render payload has no field to carry that offset and doc §map_render simultaneously asserts 'the raster IS the canvas (no separate outline frame → ro_* = the canvas, ro_dx/dy = 0)'. Those two statements in the same doc cannot both hold if the trim is nonzero. docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4 restates the ro_* = canvas claim without independent evidence.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

findings.title: Two functions in this module read the same `flip_y` key with OPPOSITE defaults, so a decoded dict missing the key renders flipped but drift-checks unflipped
findings.what_code_does: roborock_render_data reads `bool(decoded.get('flip_y', True))` (line 174) — default True. raster_room_bboxes reads `bool(decoded.get('flip_y'))` (line 198) — no default, so a missing key yields False. Same key, same module, same `decoded` dict shape, opposite absent-means semantics. This is the 'absent is not zero' pattern: the drift validator treats a missing orientation flag as 'not flipped' while the renderer treats it as 'flipped'.
findings.reproduction: Run against the shipped module with `d = {'width': 2, 'height': 3, 'room_pixels': bytes([5,5,0,0,0,0])}` (flip_y key absent), room 5 occupying raw row 0 only. raster_room_bboxes(d) returns {5: [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.3333]}; with 'flip_y': True present it returns {5: [0.0, 0.6667, 1.0, 1.0]}. roborock_render_data(d)['flip_y'] is True for the SAME dict. The two boxes do not intersect, so _bbox_iou is exactly 0.0 and geometry_drift reports min_iou 0.0 / aligned False.
findings.user_impact: Latent today: decode_roborock_v1_segments unconditionally sets flip_y True (line 126), so no shipped path produces a dict without the key. It bites the first time anything else builds a decoded dict — a b01/Qrevo decoder (the doc names b01 as the expected next format), a test fixture, or a future refactor that makes the flag conditional. The failure mode is maximally misleading: geometry_drift reports the exact 'inverted axis = a flip bug' signature that docs/dev/29 tells the maintainer to trust as evidence of a decode fault, when in fact the raster and the render agree and only the validator disagrees with itself.
findings.guards_checked: decode_roborock_v1_segments:126 always sets flip_y True (this is what makes it unreachable today, not any guard in the consumers). No shared accessor or constant derives the default from one place — each function hand-writes its own. geometry_drift:259 passes `decoded` straight through with no normalization. No test covers a decoded dict lacking flip_y (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py builds every fixture from decode_roborock_v1_segments or a literal with flip_y set).
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render / §Drift-check — states 'raw row 0 is the image BOTTOM → flip_y True' as an invariant of the v1 format and calls out that getting the flip wrong makes the two frames 'sit a whole Y-flip apart and never overlap'. The doc names the failure this divergence would manufacture, which is why a false positive here is expensive.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

findings.title: geometry_drift reports max_center_delta: 0.0 when there are no common rooms — an optimistic accumulator that survives an empty loop
findings.what_code_does: `max_center = 0.0` and `min_iou = 1.0` are initialised before the per-room loop (lines 269-271). When `common` is empty the loop never runs. `min_iou` gets the correct treatment on output — `round(min_iou, 3) if common else 0.0` (line 285) — but `max_center` does not: line 284 emits `round(max_center, 4)` unconditionally, so the optimistic pre-loop 0.0 is published as a measurement.
findings.reproduction: geometry_drift(parser_rooms=[{'number': 16, 'bbox': [0,0,.5,.5]}, {'number': 17, 'bbox': [.5,0,1,.5]}], decoded=<a raster whose rids do not overlap those ids, or an all-background raster>) yields {'room_ids_parser': [16,17], 'room_ids_raster': [], 'common': [], 'only_parser': [16,17], 'only_raster': [], 'max_center_delta': 0.0, 'min_iou': 0.0, 'aligned': False, 'per_room': {}}. max_center_delta reads as a perfect centre match on a comparison that compared nothing.
findings.user_impact: Diagnostics-readability only. The drift block is the tool a maintainer reads to decide whether the Roborock decode is correct on a real device; 'max_center_delta: 0.0' next to 'aligned: false' invites reading the geometry as fine and the room-id sets as the sole problem. It compounds the already-reported A4-RB-5 (present: True regardless of verdict, map_source_runtime.py:427). No user-facing behaviour changes and nothing gates on the value.
findings.guards_checked: geometry_drift:285 — the `if common else 0.0` ternary exists and is applied to min_iou, so the empty-loop case WAS considered; max_center at :284 is the sibling that did not get it. `aligned` at :286-289 does start with `bool(common)`, so the verdict itself is correct — only the reported metric is not. raster_room_bboxes returns {} for an empty/absent raster, which is what produces the empty intersection.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §'Surfaced in diagnostics' documents the block's exact field list including max_center_delta and instructs the reader to 'read the deltas' when not aligned. That instruction is what makes the phantom 0.0 misleading.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

findings.title: The IMAGE-block dimension guard is `header_len >= 16`, but the four dims occupy the LAST 16 bytes of a header whose first 8 are the fixed type/len fields — anything under 24 reads dims out of the header's own metadata
findings.what_code_does: Line 96 gates the dim reads on `header_len >= 16`, then reads top/left/height/width at `pos + header_len - 16 .. -4` (lines 97-100). The block header's first 8 bytes are fixed: type (int16 @0x00), header_len (int16 @0x02), data_len (int32 @0x04). So the four dim int32s only occupy bytes the format actually reserves for them when `header_len >= 24` — which is what the real v1 layout uses (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:45-55 builds exactly a 24-byte header with dims at offsets 8/12/16/20 == header_len-16/-12/-8/-4). For header_len in 16..23 the guard passes and the reads slide backwards over the type/header_len/data_len fields.
findings.reproduction: A block with type=2, header_len=20, data_len=D: `top = _u32(raw, pos+4)` == D (the data_len field re-read as a coordinate), `left = _u32(raw, pos+8)`, `height = _u32(raw, pos+12)`, `width = _u32(raw, pos+16)`. With header_len=16: `top = _u32(raw, pos+0)` == type | (header_len << 16) == 2 | 0x100000. The values are then carried into `image` (line 101) and, if `width*height <= data_len` and `data_start + width*height <= n` happen to hold, into a returned raster with garbage dims — no further sanity check exists.
findings.user_impact: Not reachable on a well-formed v1 blob (roborock uses >= 24-byte IMAGE headers). It matters as the module's stated defence posture: the docstring at lines 14-16 says the byte walk is 'mirrored from vacuum-map-parser-roborock ... so a firmware format change is a one-file fix', and a firmware/format change is precisely the event that would present a short header. A `>= 24` guard would reject it as unparseable (returning None, which the caller degrades cleanly); `>= 16` accepts it and can emit a plausible-shaped raster built on coordinates read out of the header's own length fields. The other unchecked-offset risks in this walk are genuinely covered (see clean_areas) — this is the one gate that is looser than the format it guards.
findings.guards_checked: decode_roborock_v1_segments:91 `header_len < 8 or pos + header_len > n` — bounds the read but says nothing about whether 16 bytes of DIMS fit after the 8 bytes of fixed fields. Lines 111-114 (`width<=0 or height<=0`, `pixel_count > data_len`, `data_start + pixel_count > n`) reject most garbage but are satisfiable by chance — none of them cross-checks the dims against anything independent. resolve_rid / the LUT cannot detect it. There is no minimum/maximum plausible-dimension check anywhere in the module.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render 'v1 only' spells out the layout: 'IMAGE block type == 2; top/left/height/width = int32 @ header[header_len-16..-4]' and the module docstring lines 18-25 repeat it — both describe the offsets relative to header_len without stating the minimum header_len that makes them valid, which is how the off-by-8 guard slipped in.
findings.brands_affected: roborock

clean_areas: `_u16` / `_u32` (lines 45-50) — little-endian unsigned reads, byte-for-byte what the module docstring and docs/dev/29 §map_render specify and what the reference parser's `_get_int16`/`_get_int32` do. No signedness assumption is made or needed downstream (top/left/height/width are all treated as unsigned, matching the reference). No endianness defect.

`resolve_rid` + `_RID_LUT` (lines 53-68) — CORRECT, including the trap the tests call out: 0x08 has room-bits 1 under a naive `>>3` but obstacle-bits 0, and the `(pixel_type & 0x07) == 7` mask rejects it. Verified the boundary arithmetic by hand: (30<<3)|7 == 0xF7 and (31<<3)|7 == 0xFF, so rid 31 is genuinely unrepresentable as a room byte — `MAX_ROOM_RID = 30` is arithmetically forced, not an off-by-one. The 256-entry LUT is BUILT from resolve_rid rather than hand-transcribed, so the fast path cannot drift from the slow path (the opposite of this codebase's hand-copied-vocabulary pattern).

Block-walk bounds arithmetic (lines 89-100) — every read is provably in-bounds. The loop condition `pos + 8 <= n` exactly covers `_u16(raw, pos)`, `_u16(raw, pos+2)`, `raw[pos+2]` and `_u32(raw, pos+4)`. The IMAGE dim reads at `pos + header_len - 16 .. -4` are covered on the high side by `pos + header_len <= n` and on the low side by `header_len >= 16` (>= 0 offset). There is no IndexError path; the `except (IndexError, ValueError)` at line 130 is belt-and-braces, not load-bearing.

Forward-progress / advance arithmetic (lines 102-106) — verified the docstring's claim rather than trusting it: `step = data_len + raw[pos+0x02]` equals `data_len + header_len` for every header_len < 256, because header_len = raw[pos+2] | raw[pos+3]<<8 and a value under 256 forces raw[pos+3] == 0, making the low byte the whole value. `pos += step` therefore lands exactly on `data_start + data_len`, the next block. `step == 0` is reachable only when data_len == 0 AND raw[pos+2] == 0, i.e. header_len is a multiple of 256 — and that case breaks. No infinite-loop path exists.

Truncated / absent / non-bytes blob handling (lines 79-114) — a truncated IMAGE block is correctly REJECTED, which was the headline hunt: the header can survive intact while the payload is cut, and `data_start + pixel_count > n` (line 113) catches exactly that. `pixel_count > data_len` (line 111) rejects a header claiming more pixels than the block declares. `n < 4` returns None. A non-bytes input raises TypeError/ValueError inside `bytes(raw)` and returns None; the one input that slips past that — an int, where `bytes(5)` yields five zero bytes rather than raising — still falls out as None via `header_len < 8`. None, b'', b'\x00', and random bytes all return None (confirmed by tests RRD-4 and by inspection).

`raster_room_bboxes` flip normalization (lines 218-221) — proven by arithmetic, not accepted. Raw rows [b1..b3] inclusive map to rendered rows [h-1-b3 .. h-1-b1], normalized to [(h-b3-1)/h, (h-b1)/h]; the code emits `1-(b3+1)/h` and `1-b1/h`, identical. The non-flip branch is the plain inclusive→exclusive conversion. This matches the reference parser's write order (raw row i → image row height-1-i) and is the exact inverse of the card's `pyN = (H-1) - ny*H` at src/state/map.js:953. Correct in both branches.

`_bbox_iou` (lines 225-236) — degenerate and non-overlapping boxes are handled: `max(0.0, ...)` clamps negative extents, `inter <= 0` short-circuits before any division, and `union > 0` guards the final divide. No ZeroDivisionError and no negative IoU is producible.

`geometry_drift` input coercion (lines 250-258) — hostile input from `rooms_from_mapdata` is handled without raising and without coercing to a wrong number: non-dict entries, a missing/None `number`, a non-list or wrong-length bbox, and non-numeric bbox values are each skipped via explicit isinstance/len/try-except rather than defaulted. `min_iou` correctly reports 0.0 rather than the optimistic pre-loop 1.0 when `common` is empty (line 285), and `aligned` correctly starts with `bool(common)` so an empty comparison can never read as aligned.

Payload/consumer vocabulary contract — the emitted decode params (`rid_shift`, `catch_all_rid`, `flip_y`, `ro_width/ro_height/ro_dx/ro_dy`) are all READ FROM THE PAYLOAD by every consumer (src/bindings/map.js:276-279 and :360-364 and :450-454, src/state/map.js:958-965), with no hand-copied constants on the consumer side. That is why Eufy's catch_all 32 / rid_shift 2 and Roborock's 31 / 0 coexist correctly through one brand-agnostic decoder — the question is centralized rather than the vocabulary duplicated.

Purity / no read-path mutation — every function in the module is pure. Nothing writes to .storage, there is no `setdefault` into a persisted structure, no migration-on-read, and no destructive write. The falsy guards at lines 158 and 195 (`if not rp or not width or not height`) were checked specifically for the `or`-eats-a-legitimate-falsy-value pattern: the only values they can reject are an empty raster and a zero dimension, both genuinely unusable, so no legitimate 0/[]/'' is being swallowed there.

`decode_roborock_v1_segments` cost profile — unlike raster_room_bboxes (ROBORO-2), the decode itself touches the raster only through `bytes.translate` and `set()`, and roborock_render_data only through `b64encode` and `sha1`. All C-level, so the render path's 'in-memory + pure -> loop-safe' claim at map_source_coordinator.py:620 holds for the path it actually covers.

The 5-bit raster field caps rid at 31 and 31 is the MAP_INSIDE sentinel, so such a room could not be represented in the raster at all — but I could not establish from source whether the firmware can assign one, and roborock_render_data discards decode's `room_ids` so no cross-check against the discovered room set exists either way. Flagging as an open question rather than a finding.

findings.title: map_id is documented as optional + auto-resolving on 6 presentation services but is vol.Required; a literal blank map_id silently mints and writes a phantom map bucket
findings.what_code_does: Every write handler in this block reads `map_id: str = call.data["map_id"]` (2108, 2150, 2195, 1943, 2010, 2053) and hands it straight to `ensure_map_bucket()`. Their schemas declare `vol.Required("map_id"): cv.string`. None of them calls `services/_common.py::resolved_call_data()`, the shared helper whose docstring states "the map_id field is optional on every service that takes one" and which explicitly handles the blank-string case; that helper is wired into 58 call sites across 9 modules in services/*.py and ZERO times in mapping_services.py. `_handle_set_map_overlay_visibility` (2242-2257) is the lone handler in this block that resolves an absent map_id — the forgotten-sibling shape exactly. `cv.string("")` returns "", and `ensure_map_bucket` does `data["maps"][vac].setdefault(str(map_id), {...})`, so "" mints a real, persisted bucket.
findings.reproduction: Read the machine-readable service definition the HA Actions UI renders: services.yaml declares, for set_hidden_regions / set_area_label_anchor / set_live_map_rotation / set_furnished_art_placement / set_furnished_render_mode / set_room_viewport, `map_id: required: false` with the description "Leave blank to use the current active map." (A) Omit map_id: voluptuous rejects with `required key not provided @ data['map_id']` — the documented optional parameter does not exist. (B) Follow the description literally from a script/automation: `service: eufy_vacuum.set_live_map_rotation` with `{vacuum_entity_id: vacuum.x10, map_id: "", rotation: 90}`. cv.string accepts ""; ensure_map_bucket creates `data["maps"]["vacuum.x10"][""] = {map_id:"", metadata:{}, rooms:{}, summary:{}}`; the handler writes `live_map_rotation: 90` there, async_saves, and returns `{"saved": true, "live_map_rotation": 90}`. Every reader (get_dashboard_snapshot reads `.get(str(map_id), {})` for the REAL active map; get_map_segments likewise) never looks at bucket "", so the map never rotates. Same for a hidden-region set, an area-label drag, and all three furnished writes.
findings.user_impact: The service reports success and the setting is permanently invisible — the classic silent-wrong-answer shape. It also leaves a ghost map in .storage that surfaces through get_vacuum_maps / diagnostics as an extra map with 0 rooms, and becomes a candidate for the `next(iter(vac_maps))` fallback in FURNIS-2. Blast radius is bounded: the card always sends a map_id (state/rooms.js activeMapId() falls back to "1" and can never return falsy), so only automation/script/Dev-Tools callers are affected. Branch (A) fails loudly and merely makes the published API wrong; branch (B) is the silent one. Fix is one line per handler (route through resolved_call_data, which already rejects the blank case correctly) — but see FURNIS-2 before copying its last-resort behaviour.
findings.guards_checked: voluptuous schemas (SET_HIDDEN_REGIONS_SCHEMA / SET_AREA_LABEL_ANCHOR_SCHEMA / SET_LIVE_MAP_ROTATION_SCHEMA / SET_FURNISHED_*_SCHEMA / SET_ROOM_VIEWPORT_SCHEMA) — all use cv.string, which accepts "" (it only rejects None/list/dict); ensure_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:10-28) — mints unconditionally, no existence or shape validation; rooms/room_discovery.get_active_map_id — correctly returns None on sentinel states via is_blank_state, but is never called by these handlers; the card's activeMapId() — never emits blank, so it does not rescue a hand-written call.
findings.doc_checked: docs/advanced/03-services.md (states `map_id | Yes | Required — not auto-resolved.` for all six, and explicitly calls out set_map_overlay_visibility as the one exception — this doc matches the code); custom_components/eufy_vacuum/services.yaml (states required:false + "Leave blank to use the current active map" for all six — contradicts the code); docs/dev/frontend/backend-contract-and-data-shapes.md lines 234-238 ("Optional: map_id (defaults to the active map)" for set_live_map_rotation / set_hidden_regions / set_area_label_anchor — also contradicts the code); docs/dev/17-map-manager.md §188 (documents the on-demand key writes, silent on map_id validation).
findings.brands_affected: both

findings.title: set_map_overlay_visibility's last-resort map resolution guesses the first stored map and reports saved:true against it
findings.what_code_does: When map_id is absent and get_active_map_id returns None (sentinel/unavailable active-map sensor, or the boot window where the sensor is registered but has no state — both explicit return-None paths in room_discovery), the handler falls back to `map_id = next(iter(vac_maps), None)` — the first key in `data["maps"][vacuum_entity_id]` by dict insertion order. It then ensure_map_buckets that id, writes the visibility delta, and returns `{"saved": True, "map_id": <guessed>, "overlay_visibility": <resolved>}`.
findings.reproduction: A vacuum with two maps: `data["maps"]["vacuum.x10"] = {"1": {...upstairs...}, "2": {...downstairs...}}`, currently on map "2". During the post-restart window sensor.x10_active_map is "unknown", so get_active_map_id returns None. Call `eufy_vacuum.set_map_overlay_visibility {vacuum_entity_id: vacuum.x10, visibility: {no_go: true}}`. next(iter(...)) yields "1"; the delta is written to the UPSTAIRS bucket and the response is `{saved: true, map_id: "1", overlay_visibility: {...no_go: true...}}`. The map actually being displayed ("2") is unchanged, and the pref silently appears on the other map later.
findings.user_impact: A display-only preference lands on a map the caller never named, reported as a success. Bounded: the card always supplies map_id (activeMapId() never returns falsy), so this needs a hand-written call on a multi-map vacuum during a blank-active-map window — an edge case. Recorded mainly because FURNIS-1's fix will wire five more services into map_id resolution: the shared resolved_call_data helper deliberately does NOT guess (its docstring: "silent fallback to a wrong map would be worse"), and this handler's extra guess should not be propagated with it. FURNIS-1's phantom "" bucket is also a valid next(iter(...)) winner.
findings.guards_checked: get_active_map_id (rooms/room_discovery.py:43-88) — its three documented return-None paths are exactly the ones that reach this fallback; the `if not map_id: return {saved: False, error: "no_map"}` guard at 2252 — only fires when the vacuum has NO maps at all, so it never catches the wrong-map case; the response's `map_id` echo — the card's setMapOverlayVisibility (src/actions/map.js:402-412) does its optimistic flip and never reconciles against the returned map_id.
findings.doc_checked: docs/advanced/03-services.md ("Auto-resolves to the active map (then the first stored map) when omitted") and the schema comment at the SET_MAP_OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_SCHEMA definition — the behaviour IS documented; reported as a hazard to the FURNIS-1 fix rather than an undocumented defect. services/_common.py resolved_call_data docstring documents the opposite (and safer) contract for every other service.
findings.brands_affected: both

findings.title: _handle_set_room_viewport is the only furnished writer with no clamp and a corner-valued default — zoom:0 and cx/cy:0.0 persist verbatim
findings.what_code_does: The viewport write is `{"cx": _round4(cx, 0.0), "cy": _round4(cy, 0.0), "zoom": _round4(zoom, 1.0)}` — no range clamp on any of the three. Forty lines above, the sibling in the same wave clamps scale to [0.05, 20] with a comment stating precisely why: "A raw 0 (or negative) would persist as 0.0 but the renderer coerces it back to 1x (`Number(scale) || 1`), so state and render would silently disagree; clamp here so the stored value is always renderable." Thirty lines below, `_handle_set_area_label_anchor` clamps pct to 0-100 and defaults a missing coordinate to 50.0 (centre). The viewport handler inherits neither guard, and its missing-coordinate default is 0.0 — a CORNER of the same 0-100 pct frame, not a centre.
findings.reproduction: Room 7 has a saved viewport `{cx: 72.0, cy: 41.0, zoom: 2.5}`. (a) Partial update: `set_room_viewport {room_id: "7", zoom: 3.0}` — zoom is not None so the else-branch runs and stores `{cx: 0.0, cy: 0.0, zoom: 3.0}`; the framing snaps from the room's centre to the top-left corner of the map, and the old cx/cy are gone with no undo. (b) Degenerate zoom: `set_room_viewport {room_id: "7", cx: 50, cy: 50, zoom: 0}` stores `zoom: 0.0` — the exact value the sibling's comment says must never be persisted; a consumer doing `Number(zoom) || 1` renders 1x while storage says 0, and one dividing by zoom gets a ZeroDivisionError/Infinity. (c) Out of frame: `{cx: -400, cy: 9000, zoom: -3}` round-trips verbatim through resolve_furnished_render into the snapshot.
findings.user_impact: Latent today — say so plainly: docs/advanced/08-map-configuration.md line 270 records the per-room viewport as "service-only today, not yet a panel control", and the card reads no viewport (src/state/map.js: "Per-room art / sub-tabs / saved viewport are Wave 2 — NOT read or written here"), so nothing renders it yet. The cost is that unrenderable values are being accepted and persisted NOW, so a Wave-2 consumer inherits a store the two sibling writers were explicitly hardened against, and any automation-authored viewport is already silently mis-stored.
findings.guards_checked: _round4 (1930-1932) — rounds only, no range logic, and its `default` fires on None so it cannot distinguish 'omitted' from 'explicitly null'; SET_ROOM_VIEWPORT_SCHEMA — vol.Any(None, vol.Coerce(float)) with no vol.Range, unlike SET_AREA_LABEL_ANCHOR's services.yaml selector which at least declares min:0/max:100; the missing-room_id guard at 2059 (catches a blank id, nothing about values); resolve_furnished_render (map_source.py:126) — passes `viewport` through untouched by contract.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md lines 213-233 (documents transforms/viewports as pct floats and calls out only `scale` as clamped [0.05, 20] — silent on zoom); docs/advanced/03-services.md §set_room_viewport (documents only the all-null clear); tests/integration/test_mapping_furnished_render.py FURN-7 covers all-three-set and all-null but no partial and no degenerate value, while FURN-16 exists specifically to pin the scale clamp on the sibling.
findings.brands_affected: both

findings.title: area_label_anchors are keyed by device room id and nothing prunes them on a room rebuild, so a re-import silently re-aims one room's dragged label onto a different room
findings.what_code_does: `anchors: dict = map_bucket.setdefault("area_label_anchors", {})` then `anchors[room_id] = {pct_x, pct_y}`, keyed by the raw device room id, at the MAP-BUCKET level. The room set that gives those ids meaning is rebuilt by `maps/map_manager.py::rebuild_map_bucket`, which at line 201 does `map_bucket["rooms"] = rebuilt_rooms` — a wholesale replacement that drops rooms no longer discovered — and touches nothing else. Grepping maps/ and rooms/ for `area_label_anchors` / `companion_anchors` returns zero hits: no prune, no reconcile, no fingerprint of which room set an anchor was authored against.
findings.reproduction: Map "1" has rooms 1..6; room 3 is the Kitchen. The user drags the Kitchen m² chip clear of its name label to the room's right edge: `area_label_anchors["3"] = {pct_x: 78.5, pct_y: 22.0}`. The vacuum is factory-reset / re-mapped (this project's own device notes record Eufy re-issuing room ids 1..N from scratch); rediscovery calls rebuild_map_bucket, which replaces `rooms` — now room 3 is the Bedroom on the opposite side of the house. `area_label_anchors["3"]` is still `{78.5, 22.0}` and the dashboard snapshot hands it out verbatim (core/manager.py:4176-4179), so the Bedroom's m² chip renders at 78.5%/22.0% of the map content box — over the Kitchen, detached from its room and possibly overlapping another room's label. A room that vanished entirely (say old room 6) keeps its anchor in storage forever.
findings.user_impact: This is the direct answer to 'does the edit survive a re-import?': the bytes survive, their meaning does not, and nothing detects it. Cosmetic in consequence (a mis-placed m² chip, not a mis-cleaned room) but silently wrong and non-obvious — the user cannot tell that a chip is stale rather than mis-rendered. Reversible only by noticing and re-dragging (or calling the service with both pcts null). The same shape applies to the map-level `companion_anchors` and to each custom layout's furnished `rooms` map, which are keyed the same way and equally unpruned.
findings.guards_checked: rebuild_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:109-250) — replaces `rooms` and `summary`, preserves per-room settings via RoomConfig, and never looks at the sibling UI-state keys; the `preserve_existing_settings` flag — governs room records only; the dashboard snapshot reader (core/manager.py:4176) — isinstance-guards the type and copies the dict, but does no key validation against the live room list; the write handler itself — no room-existence check (consistent with _handle_set_segment_room_link / _handle_set_companion_anchor, so this is a family-wide gap rather than one forgotten site).
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md lines 130-135 and 363 (documents `{room_id: {pct_x, pct_y}}` and the null-both reset; silent on lifecycle vs the room set); docs/dev/17-map-manager.md §188 (states these keys are written on demand and consumers must read them defensively — no invalidation contract); docs/advanced/03-services.md §set_area_label_anchor (same, storage-only description).
findings.brands_affected: both

findings.title: hidden_regions are stored as normalized rects with no record of the frame they were authored against, so a re-map re-aims the masks onto different physical areas — and masks hide content by default
findings.what_code_does: The handler sanitizes each rect and replace-alls them into `map_bucket["hidden_regions"]` as normalized 0-1 of the RENDERED IMAGE. That is the only thing stored: no image_size, no map fingerprint, no authored-at stamp, no schema version. The reader hands them back unconditionally (core/manager.py:4180-4183 for the dashboard, plus the get_map_segments payload), and the card places them with the same letterbox transform the device overlays use (src/renderers/map.js::_renderHiddenRegions), painting background-coloured rects at z-index 5 — above room labels AND area chips — with `hidden_regions` defaulting to visible:true in OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_DEFAULTS.
findings.reproduction: Arithmetic: the user masks porch noise sitting at columns 80-95 of a 100-column rendered map → stored `[0.80, 0.10, 0.95, 0.25]`. The robot later discovers a new area to the east and the rendered extent grows to 130 columns covering the same house plus 30 new columns. The same physical porch now sits at 80/130 = 0.615 to 95/130 = 0.731. The stored rect is unchanged, so it is now drawn at columns 0.80*130 = 104 through 0.95*130 = 123.5 — inside the newly discovered area. The porch reappears and a slice of the new room is covered by an opaque background-coloured rect that also swallows its label and m² chip. map_id is unchanged across the re-map, so the same bucket is reused and nothing signals a mismatch. Provable from code: no fingerprint is written at 2130 and no consumer validates one. The premise that the rendered extent changes across a re-map is device behaviour (sharpest on Roborock, whose map image is trimmed to the occupied bounding box) and is what needs a hardware check.
findings.user_impact: Map content silently disappears with no indication of why, on a map the user never edited — the mask looks like a rendering bug rather than stale state. Recovery exists but is undiscoverable unless the user remembers the Hide-area tool: toggling the hidden_regions overlay off reveals what is under, and edit mode exposes a per-rect delete. Not destructive (nothing else is overwritten) and not a dispatch risk (masks are display-only; cleaning is by room id).
findings.guards_checked: the sanitizer at 2111-2124 — correct for the values it sees (bool/NaN/inf rejected BEFORE the clamp, which matters: max(0.0,min(1.0,nan)) evaluates to 1.0 in CPython, so the comment's claim that NaN would clamp to an edge rather than drop is accurate; degenerate <0.001 rects dropped; min<max ordered) but it validates shape, never provenance; the in-place `regions.clear()/extend()` — safe, every reader copies (`list(...)`) so no cached snapshot aliases the stored list; the card's draw gate (src/state/map.js:815) — requires an aligned backdrop and rotation 0 to DRAW a mask, but does not gate RENDERING of existing masks; the overlay-visibility toggle — a manual escape hatch, not a guard.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md lines 124-129 and 362 (defines the normalized frame and the sanitizer; silent on invalidation); docs/advanced/03-services.md §set_hidden_regions ("0-1 of the rendered image, top-left origin ... Hidden regions are physical, so they are stored at the map level and follow the map regardless of segmentation mode" — states the intent that they follow the map, without addressing the map's own frame changing); docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §648 (lists hidden_regions on the get_map_segments payload, no lifecycle).
findings.brands_affected: both — sharpest on Roborock, whose rendered image is trimmed to the occupied extent

findings.title: Clearing a home-scope art placement setdefaults an empty home_art dict, flipping the 'no furnished data' sentinel from None to a confident empty payload
findings.what_code_does: The clear path takes `target = layout.setdefault("home_art", {})` BEFORE deciding it is a clear, then pops the (absent) transform. On a layout with no art yet, that leaves `layout["home_art"] = {}` behind. The reader guards the per-room branch against exactly this — `if not any(entry.get(f) is not None for f in _FURNISHED_FIELDS): continue` skips empty room entries — but the home branch tests only `if home_art_raw is None`, and `{}` is not None. The forgotten sibling is in the reader; the writer mints the empty dict for both.
findings.reproduction: Map in custom mode with an active layout carrying no art. Call `set_furnished_art_placement {scope: "home"}` with no coordinates. Response: `{saved: true, action: "cleared", furnished_render: {...}}` — and resolve_furnished_render, which returned None a moment earlier ('the map has no furnished data'), now returns `{active_layout_id: ..., render_mode: "live", home_art: {art_url: None, transform: None}, rooms: {}}`, both in that response and in every subsequent dashboard snapshot. The same setdefault-then-pop leaves permanent empty `rooms[<id>] = {}` entries via the room-scope clear (1967) and via _handle_set_room_viewport's clear (2071); those are absorbed by the reader's per-room guard but accumulate in storage with nothing to clean them.
findings.user_impact: No visible effect today: the card's clear button only renders when hasArt is true (src/renderers/map.js:1581), so the empty-home_art state is unreachable from the UI, and the current consumers key off art_url/render_mode rather than the payload's presence. It matters because `furnished_render is None` is the documented 'no furnished data' sentinel that a Wave-2 consumer is likely to branch on, and a no-op clear permanently falsifies it for that layout.
findings.guards_checked: resolve_furnished_render (map_source.py:111-137) — the `_FURNISHED_FIELDS` any()-check protects rooms only; the `if home_art_raw is None and not rooms_out: return None` early return at 129 — defeated by `{}` being non-None; _furnished_art_url — correctly returns None for a missing variant rather than raising, so nothing downstream errors; the card's hasArt gate — blocks the UI path but not the service path; test FURN-5 (test_clear_home_art_placement) — asserts only that the transform key is gone, and its setup sets a placement first, so it never exercises the mint-on-empty case.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md lines 213-233 ("They are schema-free and minted lazily — `rooms` starts `{}`; `home_art`/`render_mode` appear on first write" — an empty home_art from a CLEAR is not a 'first write' in that sense); map_source.py resolve_furnished_render docstring ("Returns None when ... the active layout carries no furnished data (no whole-home art AND no per-room furnished field)" — a claim this case falsifies); docs/dev/frontend/furnished-render.md line 27 ("All-null clears it").
findings.brands_affected: both

clean_areas: _handle_set_live_map_rotation (2184-2210) — CLEAN. `int(call.data["rotation"]) % 360` is a defensive no-op because SET_LIVE_MAP_ROTATION_SCHEMA is vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.In([0,90,180,270])); the services.yaml select sends strings ("90") which Coerce(int) handles before vol.In, so the enum cannot be bypassed. Verified the display-only claim: grepping live_map_rotation across the component finds only the write here, the snapshot echo (core/manager.py:4101), and the card — no dispatch path reads it.

_handle_acknowledge_map_frame (2213-2225) — CLEAN, and both of its docstring CLAIMS verify. (a) "the gate re-arms automatically on the next map switch": _compute_map_frame_gate (core/manager.py:4297-4310) sets gate["user_ack"]=False and gate["ungrounded"]=True on any active-map token change, so the ack genuinely expires. (b) "transient in-memory gate state only, so there is nothing to persist (no async_save)": self._map_frame_gate is a plain dict initialised at manager.py:465 and never written into self.data — correctly omitting async_save. Minor note, not raised as a finding: the handler returns acknowledged:true unconditionally even for a vacuum with no gate, but the card only surfaces the control when frame_ungrounded is true.

_handle_set_hidden_regions sanitizer (2111-2124) — CLEAN and better than it looks. Ordering is load-bearing and correct: bool/NaN/inf are rejected BEFORE the 0-1 clamp, and I verified in CPython that max(0.0, min(1.0, nan)) evaluates to 1.0 — so the inline comment's justification ("NaN would clamp to an edge, not drop") is accurate rather than decorative. min<max ordering via sorted(), degenerate/stray-tap rects dropped at >0.001, 5dp rounding. `raw = call.data.get("regions") or []` is NOT an or-coercion bug here: the schema supplies default=list and an empty list clearing everything is the documented contract. The in-place clear()/extend() on the stored list is safe — the dashboard snapshot copies with list(...) (manager.py:4180), so no previously-emitted payload aliases it.

_handle_set_map_overlay_visibility delta merge (2263-2277) — CLEAN. Stores only deltas, resolves over OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_DEFAULTS at read time, non-dict stored value is coerced to {} rather than trusted, values are bool()-normalised, reset pops the key. The schema validates layer names with vol.Schema({vol.In(tuple(OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_DEFAULTS)): cv.boolean}) so a typo'd layer is rejected instead of silently stored — the one place in this block where hand-copied vocabulary was correctly derived from the single source. reset:true + visibility together is unambiguous (reset wins) and the response reports the true resolved result.

_handle_set_furnished_render_mode blank-room_id routing (2023-2031) — CLEAN and deliberately divergent from its siblings. A blank/whitespace room_id routes to the LAYOUT level instead of being rejected, the comment explains why the placement/viewport handlers reject the same input, and test FURN-15 pins it as a regression guard (including that no phantom rooms[""] entry is minted). This is the 'centralize the question, not the vocabulary' shape done right — the divergence is genuine, not an oversight.

_round4 (1930-1932) — the docstring claim "schema already did [the float coercion]" verifies against both SET_FURNISHED_ART_PLACEMENT_SCHEMA and SET_ROOM_VIEWPORT_SCHEMA (vol.Any(None, vol.Coerce(float))). The scale clamp at 1982-1984 and its stated reason (the renderer's `Number(scale) || 1` would disagree with a persisted 0) are correct and pinned by test FURN-16. Note the partial-write default behaviour on art placement (only tx set -> ty/scale/rotation written as 0/1/0) is NOT reported as a finding: test FURN-3 asserts it explicitly as intended, so it is a decided design, not a forgotten guard — see FURNIS-3 for where the same shape was NOT decided.

Per-layout scoping of all three furnished writes (1961, 2019, 2067) — CLEAN, and the block banner's claim holds. Every furnished write resolves through _active_custom_layout and refuses with {saved:false, reason:"no_active_layout"} rather than falling back to the map bucket, so furnished state cannot leak across CV/other layouts; layout["updated_at"] is bumped on all three, matching the data-model contract that updated_at tracks furnished writes. Covered by tests FURN-8 and test_per_layout_furnished_isolation.

Concurrency — CLEAN by construction. Every handler in this block performs its whole mutation synchronously and then awaits exactly one manager.async_save(); there is no read-modify-write straddling an await. The one post-await read (resolve_furnished_render at 2000/2043/2093) re-reads the live map_bucket dict, and no code path replaces a map bucket object wholesale (rebuild_map_bucket mutates in place), so the reference cannot go stale. No two-coroutine-interleave claims apply.

The three GET delegations (2280-2308) — CLEAN as handlers: pure three-line passthroughs to manager.async_get_map_render_data / async_get_map_live_pose / async_compare_map_sources, adding no local state, no cached value and no failure swallowing. Registering get_map_live_pose and compare_map_sources against GET_MAP_RENDER_DATA_SCHEMA is schema REUSE, not a copy bug — all three take exactly {vacuum_entity_id}. Dead-code observation (not raised as a finding): _LIVE_ROOM_PROBE_TASKS at 2323 and the decapitated banner at 2311-2320 are leftovers of a removed probe, and the banner cites docs/dev/eufy-native-transition.md, which no longer exists in the repo.
not_examined: The bodies of async_get_map_render_data / async_get_map_live_pose / async_compare_map_sources — they live in mapping/map_source_coordinator.py, which is explicitly out of scope (already audited). So the brief's question 'do the three GET handlers return a confident payload when the underlying source is missing or stale?' is answered here only at the handler layer: they add no guard, no staleness envelope and no fallback of their own, and return whatever the coordinator returns verbatim. One handler-layer observation worth passing to whoever owns the coordinator: none of the three accepts a map_id — they are scoped to a vacuum, so the payload (including the `version` the card caches by) always describes whatever map the coordinator picks. Not reachable as a bug today because the card only ever displays activeMapId(), but it means the card cannot ask for a named map's raster.

resolve_furnished_render and resolve_overlay_visibility bodies (mapping/map_source.py:55-144) — read as evidence for FURNIS-6 and for the overlay-delta merge, but map_source.py is out of scope and no finding is filed against it. FURNIS-6 is filed against the WRITER's setdefault, which is in scope; the reader-side asymmetry is described only as corroboration.

core/manager.py get_dashboard_snapshot (3905-4200) and _compute_map_frame_gate / acknowledge_map_frame (4275-4347) — read to verify read-path behaviour and to check the acknowledge_map_frame docstring claims, not reviewed for their own defects.

maps/map_manager.py rebuild_map_bucket — read only far enough to establish that it replaces map_bucket['rooms'] wholesale and prunes no sibling UI-state key (the mechanism behind FURNIS-4). Its own documented BUG-B (reduced 4-key summary entry) is already tracked in docs/dev/00-disaster-recovery-standard.md and is not re-reported.

Frontend files (src/actions/map.js, src/state/map.js, src/state/rooms.js, src/renderers/map.js, src/bindings/map.js) — read purely to establish reachability of each finding from the card (notably that activeMapId() can never return falsy, and that the furnished clear/save buttons are gated on hasArt). Not reviewed for card-side defects.

The other 51 services whose services.yaml entry declares map_id optional. I verified that services/*.py routes 58 call sites through resolved_call_data and that mapping_services.py routes zero, but I only confirmed the code-vs-services.yaml divergence for the six services inside my line range. The same divergence plausibly affects the other mapping_services.py handlers (set_segment_room_link, set_companion_anchor, upload/delete_map_image, the layout and saved-zone CRUD) — those lines belong to other reviewers.
The saved-zone banner claim at line 2472 flagged in the brief — outside my line range (1918-2326), not examined.

findings.title: set_custom_segments is a REPLACE-ALL write that cannot name its target layout — it lands on whatever layout is active at call time, destroying another layout's authored geometry
findings.what_code_does: _handle_set_custom_segments takes only (vacuum_entity_id, map_id, segments[, backdrop_width/height]) — SET_CUSTOM_SEGMENTS_SCHEMA (line 378-397) and services.yaml both have NO layout_id field. The target is resolved server-side from global state at line 1667 (`layout = _ensure_default_layout(map_bucket)` -> `_active_custom_layout` -> `map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id']`), then line 1710 does `layout['custom_segments'] = {...}` — a full replace of that layout's authored polygons with no merge, no confirmation, no undo, and no prior-value capture. The card's compose-save (src/bindings/map.js:1382-1421) then loops `set_segment_room_link(mapId, seg.id, ...)` once per segment — also layout-less, also resolved through _resolve_active_scope at call time. Contrast the sibling writer _handle_upload_map_image (line 849-875), which REQUIRES layout_id and returns {'saved': false, 'reason': 'layout_not_found'} if it does not resolve: the identity guard exists in this file, but only on the non-destructive path.
findings.reproduction: Two card instances on the same map (wall tablet + phone — normal HA usage). (1) Tablet is in custom mode on layout 'Upstairs' (active), user composes 6 shapes. (2) Phone user taps the layout picker for 'Downstairs' -> set_active_custom_layout -> map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id'] = downstairs_id. (3) Tablet taps Save. set_custom_segments resolves the active layout = Downstairs and overwrites Downstairs' custom_segments with the 6 Upstairs shapes; the following set_segment_room_link loop writes Upstairs' room links into Downstairs' links dict (and its 1:1 rule at line 1843-1846 POPS Downstairs' own links for each colliding room). Result: 'Upstairs' unchanged (the user believes it saved), 'Downstairs' authored geometry gone. Single-client variant: the Save button is disabled while busy (src/renderers/map.js:1527) but the layout-picker buttons are NOT — tapping another layout during the multi-await save (set_custom_segments, then N awaited set_segment_room_link calls, each awaiting manager.async_save()) splits one save across two layouts. That is a gap ACROSS awaits inside a single HA event loop, not an interleaving fantasy.
findings.user_impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of hand-authored map geometry plus its room links. The layout the user was editing is left untouched and the one they were not looking at is destroyed; the service returns {'saved': True, 'segment_count': N} either way, so nothing surfaces. Requires either two clients or an in-flight layout switch — the single-client, single-tab path is fine.
findings.guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — guarantees SOME layout exists, never that it is the intended one; the card's _composeLoadedFor/_composeKey (src/state/map.js:1418) — client-side only, keyed on the LAST fetched active_custom_layout_id, never re-validated before saving and never sent to the server; _handle_upload_map_image's layout_not_found validation — present, but only on the upload path; manager.async_save() — persists, no optimistic-concurrency token or version check anywhere in the bucket; the `if not res?.saved` check in the card binding — only catches no_custom_backdrop, not wrong-target.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 + §10.4 ('rebuilds the **active layout's** custom_segments store from scratch each call (replace-all)') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'The active-scope seam' ('set_custom_segments targets the active layout'). The docs calmly DESCRIBE active-layout targeting; neither states that the client is unable to name the layout, and neither reconciles it with §10.3, which requires layout_id on the far less destructive upload path. services.yaml:2449-2457 is additionally stale — it says the call 'Rebuilds the map's custom segment set' (no mention of layouts at all) and 'Requires a custom backdrop image', which the live-dims path at line 1673-1682 has superseded.
findings.brands_affected: Both (Eufy + Roborock) — custom layouts are brand-independent map-bucket state.

findings.title: In custom mode with no resolvable layout, _resolve_active_scope hands writers THROWAWAY dicts — set_companion_anchor / set_segment_room_link mutate a garbage-collected object and report saved: True
findings.what_code_does: _resolve_active_scope's no-layout branch (lines 1550-1554) returns freshly-constructed `{}` literals for segments_store/links/anchors. They are not reachable from manager.data. _handle_set_companion_anchor (line 1890) binds `anchors = _resolve_active_scope(map_bucket)['anchors']`, writes `anchors[room_id] = {...}`, calls `await manager.async_save()` (which serialises manager.data — the anchor is not in it), and returns `{'saved': True, 'action': 'set', 'companion_anchors': {<the anchor>}}`. _handle_set_segment_room_link (line 1834) does the same for links. The third writer through the same seam, _handle_set_custom_segments, DOES call _ensure_default_layout first (line 1667) — the guard exists and was wired into one of the three siblings.
findings.reproduction: Reachable from the shipped card with no scripting. (1) A map with zero custom layouts. (2) User taps the Custom toggle: src/bindings/map.js:1228 -> set_segmentation_mode(mode='custom'). _handle_set_segmentation_mode line 1342-1345 soft-selects a layout only `if layouts:` — with `custom_layouts == {}` the branch is skipped, so the bucket is left at segmentation_mode='custom', active_custom_layout_id=None. (3) get_map_segments now serves segments=[] and companion_anchors={}. (4) The vacuum is docked, so the renderer falls through `if (!targetSeg) return this._mapAnimalDeviceFallback(...)` (src/renderers/map.js:1008) and draws the mascot with anchorKey='dock' — draggable. (5) User drags the mascot to park it. src/bindings/map.js:1944 optimistically updates local state and fires set_companion_anchor(mapId, 'dock', x, y), ignoring the response. Server writes into the throwaway dict, saves nothing, answers saved: True.
findings.user_impact: The mascot visibly stays where the user parked it for the rest of the session (the card never refetches after an anchor write) and silently snaps back on the next page load — repeatedly, with no error and no way for the user to tell the write failed. The same hole applies to set_segment_room_link for any script/automation caller. This is a result-returning API whose failure is not merely discarded but actively reported as success.
findings.guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — the fix, wired into set_custom_segments only, absent from both other writers; _handle_set_segmentation_mode's soft-select (line 1342-1345) — gated on `if layouts:`, so it does not cover the zero-layout case that creates the state; _handle_delete_custom_layout's reassign-or-flip-to-cv (line 2422-2432) — covers deleting the last layout but not a map that never had one; _migrate_custom_layouts — seeds custom_layouts={} + active=None and returns, which is exactly the vulnerable state; the card's `if (!res?.saved)` check exists on compose-save but not on the anchor/link calls.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 states 'When no layout resolves, empty **read-only** stores are returned' — the author knew these dicts were not writable, yet two of the three writers that consume the seam mutate them and report success. docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AnchorRecord' documents the dock anchor as persisted per-scope. Code/doc divergence either way: the doc says read-only, the code lets writers write.
findings.brands_affected: Both (Eufy + Roborock). The card path additionally needs a live map source present (mss.present) for the dock-mascot fallback, which is the normal Eufy fork configuration.

findings.title: _backfill_saved_zone_area fails OPEN on an indeterminate active map and permanently persists area_m2 / room_number computed from the WRONG map's raster — the poisoned value never self-heals
findings.what_code_does: Line 1449: `if not (active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)): return False` — i.e. an indeterminate active map PROCEEDS ('Indeterminate active map -> attempt'). It then calls `manager.async_get_map_data_dict(vacuum_entity_id=...)`, which returns the fork's currently-cached map_data for whatever map is loaded, with no map-identity field to cross-check against map_id. The derived area_m2 / room_number are written onto the zone (lines 1466-1469) and the caller persists them (line 1276-1279). Crucially, the `pending` filter is `z.get('area_m2') is None` (line 1434-1437), so once a wrong value is written the zone leaves the pending set FOREVER — there is no re-validation when the correct map later becomes active. get_active_map_id returns None on a blank/unavailable/unknown active-map entity and during the boot window (rooms/room_discovery.py:69-84), so 'indeterminate' is a routine transient state, not an exotic one.
findings.reproduction: Multi-floor Eufy household. Zone 'Under the dining table' was drawn on map B while map A was loaded, so create's identical guard left area_m2=None (this is precisely the population the backfill exists to repair). HA restarts (or the vacuum drops to unavailable) -> the active-map entity is blank -> get_active_map_id returns None. The user opens the card on map B; get_map_segments -> _backfill_saved_zone_area -> guard passes (active_map_id is None) -> async_get_map_data_dict returns map A's raster. Arithmetic, using zone_membership's own formula (area = Δnx*Δny*width*height*res²/10000): zone bbox Δnx=Δny=0.10. Map A width=800 height=600 res=5 -> 0.10*800*5 = 400 cm by 0.10*600*5 = 300 cm -> 12.0 m². Map B (the zone's real map) width=400 height=300 res=5 -> 200 cm by 150 cm -> 3.0 m². The zone is stamped 12.0 m² — 4x too large — plus a room_number taken from map A's room-id raster (Eufy room ids 1-11 are per-map, so 'room 3' on A is a different physical room from 'room 3' on B). manager.async_save() persists it, and because area_m2 is now non-None the zone is never re-examined.
findings.user_impact: Permanently wrong zone size shown in the card, a zone filed under the wrong room in the browse list (grouped by room_number per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md), and a wrong area feeding the learning/duration-estimate path — which this function's own docstring claims it exists to make reliable. Irreversible from the UI: nothing recomputes area_m2 once set, so the only repair is editing .storage by hand. The single-map household is unaffected (the loaded map IS the zone's map); it needs 2+ maps plus a blank active-map entity at read time.
findings.guards_checked: The active-map guard at line 1449 itself — present, but the `active_map_id is None` arm inverts it; get_active_map_id's own sentinel handling (rooms/room_discovery.py:69) — it returns None precisely when it cannot tell, which is the arm that fails open; the create-time guard at line 2503 — identical shape, same fail-open, so the two paths agree on the wrong answer rather than one rescuing the other; map_data carries no map-id field to cross-check, and async_get_map_data_dict (map_source_coordinator.py:665) takes only vacuum_entity_id, so the callee cannot help; zone_membership is defensive but has no way to know which map it was handed; there is no re-heal path because `pending` keys on area_m2 being None.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §4 + lines 57-59 (area_m2 'computed from map dims at author time (display + validation)', room_number 'auto-set at author by >=90% dominance'); map_source.zone_membership's own docstring ('Roborock has no per-pixel raster... area_m2 needs the Eufy width/height/resolution dims'); docs/dev/10-learning-system.md:632 (zone area feeds the estimate). No doc states or defends 'when the active map is unknown, size the zone against whatever raster is loaded' — the inline comment asserts the guard 'mirrors create's guard', which is true but is a claim about consistency, not about correctness.
findings.brands_affected: Eufy only — on Roborock async_get_map_data_dict returns None early (map_source_coordinator.py:683), so nothing is written.

findings.title: _backfill_saved_zone_area overwrites a user's explicit 'Unassigned' filing — room_number=None means both 'never computed' and 'user chose Unassigned', and the read path cannot tell them apart
findings.what_code_does: Line 1467-1468: `if zone.get('room_number') is None and membership.get('room_number') is not None: zone['room_number'] = membership.get('room_number')`. The sentinel for 'not yet computed' is the same value the user's own override writes: _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2573) sets `zone['room_number'] = room_number` where SET_SAVED_ZONE_ROOM_SCHEMA (line 476-484) makes null an explicit, documented choice meaning Unassigned. There is no `filed_by`/`room_number_source` flag, no separate 'computed' key, and no boolean to distinguish the two states — classic absent-is-not-a-value conflation.
findings.reproduction: (1) Zone created while a different map was loaded, or with no map data available -> area_m2=None, room_number=None. (2) User opens the zone panel and files it under 'Kitchen' (set_saved_zone_room room_number=5). area_m2 is still None, so the zone stays in `pending`. (3) User changes their mind and picks Unassigned (set_saved_zone_room room_number=null) -> room_number=None, persisted, exactly as documented. (4) The zone's map later becomes active and the user opens the card. _backfill_saved_zone_area sees area_m2 is None -> computes membership -> sets area_m2 AND, because room_number is None, re-files the zone under the >=90%-dominant room. The user's deliberate Unassigned is gone, on a READ, with no service call from them.
findings.user_impact: A saved zone silently jumps out of the Unassigned section into a room section the user explicitly moved it out of. Filing only — docs are explicit that room_number never affects dispatch, so no wrong physical clean. Narrow: only bites zones that reached the user-editing stage while still unsized (i.e. authored off-active-map or with no map data). Once a zone has an area_m2 it is out of `pending` and immune.
findings.guards_checked: The `zone.get('room_number') is None` test at line 1467 — it IS the bug, not a guard; the `pending` filter (line 1434) — narrows the population but does not exclude user-edited zones, because a user can file/unfile a zone whose area_m2 is still None; _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2557-2576) — writes room_number and bumps updated_at but records no provenance the backfill could consult; nothing in _create_saved_zone (line 1396-1417) distinguishes a computed None from a chosen None either.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md lines 57-59 ('room_number ... auto-set at author by >=90% dominance, else None ("Unassigned"); user-editable'), line 102 ('room_number is user-settable any time (a room picker; None = Unassigned)') and line 115-116 (set_saved_zone_room, 'null = Unassigned'). The doc states the user override as a first-class, persistent choice; it never says a later read may reverse it.
findings.brands_affected: Eufy only — zone_membership returns room_number=None on Roborock (no per-pixel raster), so the `membership.get('room_number') is not None` arm never fires there.

findings.title: _generate_saved_zone_id / _generate_custom_layout_id guarantee uniqueness only against LIVE ids, so an id is reused after a delete — and saved-zone ids are durably referenced by queue steps and run profiles
findings.what_code_does: Both generators build `base = f'sz_|cl_{datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")}'` and only append `_2`, `_3`… while the candidate collides with a member of `existing`, which _create_saved_zone (line 1404) supplies as `set(zones)` — the CURRENTLY-LIVE ids of that map's saved_zones. A deleted id is not in that set, so the very next create in the same wall-clock second re-mints it. The docstrings assert these are 'Stable unique id' with a guard so 'rapid creates (and tests) never clash' — true for concurrent live ids, false across a delete. This matters because zone ids OUTLIVE the zone: core/manager.py:1736 stores `{'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': [...]}` inside the map bucket's durable queue_breaks (and run-profile steps), and _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539-2554) pops the zone without sweeping a single one of those references. Resolution is by id at dispatch time (manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects, line 1855-1878), which 'silently skips' ids it cannot find.
findings.reproduction: (1) Queue step exists: `{'after_index': 2, 'step': {'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': ['sz_20260731T142530']}}` for the zone 'Litter corner'. (2) User deletes 'Litter corner' — the queue step keeps the dead id and now silently resolves to nothing. (3) Within the same second (scripted delete+create, a double-tap flow, or a card that deletes-and-redraws) the user creates 'Under the couch'. _generate_saved_zone_id computes base='sz_20260731T142530', finds it absent from the live set, and returns it unchanged. (4) The next run reaches the queue step, _resolve_saved_zone_rects resolves 'sz_20260731T142530' to the NEW zone's bbox and dispatch_zone_clean fires it. The vacuum zone-cleans 'Under the couch' where the step said 'Litter corner'. The clock source widens this beyond one second in one case: datetime.now() is naive LOCAL time, so a DST fall-back replays a whole hour of id space.
findings.user_impact: Wrong physical area cleaned by a saved queue step or run profile, with no warning — the failure class is the most serious in this subsystem, but the window is narrow (delete and create must land in the same wall-clock second). The far more common outcome of the same missing-reference-sweep is benign: the step silently cleans nothing. Layout ids reuse the same way but nothing durable outside the bucket keys off them (the migrated layout's backdrop variant is the literal 'custom', and per-layout variants are re-derived on upload), so the layout side is latent.
findings.guards_checked: The same-second collision loop at lines 1371-1373 / 1382-1385 — only tests membership of the live `existing` set; _create_saved_zone's `set(zones)` (line 1404) — the live map's zones only, so per-map and point-in-time; _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539) — no reference sweep of queue_breaks or profile steps; manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1866-1878) — validates that the id RESOLVES and that the geometry has >=3 points, but has no way to know the id was recycled; dispatch_zone_clean's brand count/size caps — orthogonal; no uuid, no monotonic counter, no tombstone of retired ids anywhere.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'CustomLayout' ('layout_id is generated as "cl_{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS}" (with a same-second collision guard)') and docs/dev/07-queue-engine.md:575-576 (zone steps resolved at materialization via manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects over the map's saved_zones geometry). The docs describe the same-second guard as the whole uniqueness story and never state that ids must be unique over TIME, which the durable zone_ids references silently require.
findings.brands_affected: Both — saved zones and queue zone steps exist for Eufy and Roborock alike.

findings.title: adjust_map_segment persists a map-level record keyed by a segment id that CV re-analysis recycles — a nudge authored for one room silently re-attaches to whichever segment inherits that id
findings.what_code_does: Line 1752 stores the accumulated transform in `map_bucket['image_segment_adjustments'][segment_id]`, a map-level dict keyed purely by segment_id, with no fingerprint of the geometry it was authored against (no analyzed_at, no polygon hash, no bbox). CV segment ids are positional: adapters/eufy/segmentor.py:1289 mints `f'segment_{segment_id}'` from a running counter over detected components. _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) replaces `map_bucket['image_segments']` wholesale on force_reanalyze and never clears or invalidates image_segment_adjustments, and _handle_get_map_segments (line 1205-1208) blindly re-applies the old records to the new segments by id.
findings.reproduction: (1) User nudges 'segment_3' (the den) by delta_x=+40, delta_y=-25 to line its outline up with the backdrop; the record persists at image_segment_adjustments['segment_3']. (2) The robot re-explores and the user re-uploads the map image and taps Re-analyze (force_reanalyze=true). The segmenter now detects one extra component early in the scan, so the den is emitted as 'segment_4' and the hallway becomes 'segment_3'. (3) The next get_map_segments applies the stale record to the hallway: _apply_segment_adjustments shifts the hallway polygon by (+40, -25), rewrites its bbox and center_pixel, and tags it 'translated_manual' — while the den, which actually needed the nudge, renders unadjusted.
findings.user_impact: A displayed room outline is silently offset from its true position and falsely labelled as manually adjusted, and the correction the user made is lost from the room it belonged to. Display/linking only — segment polygons are not the dispatch geometry (room cleans go by room id, zone cleans by saved-zone geometry), so nothing physical goes wrong. Only bites installs that both use segment nudges and re-analyze after the map changed; a re-analyze that reproduces the same component order is harmless.
findings.guards_checked: The segment-existence check at line 1749-1750 — validates only at WRITE time and only against the current image_segments, so it cannot protect a record that outlives the segmentation it was written for; the zero-netting cleanup at line 1783-1794 — removes an entry only when the user manually nudges it back to zero; _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) — replaces image_segments and calls async_save with no adjustment invalidation; _apply_segment_adjustments (line 756-825) — matches purely on `str(seg.get('segment_id'))` with no cross-check that the polygon is the one the transform was authored against.
findings.doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AdjustmentRecord' ('CV-segment edits only — written by adjust_map_segment, applied to image_segments at read time', 'Deltas accumulate across calls') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md §image_segments ('Re-running CV re-segments and forces a relink (accepted)'). The doc explicitly accepts that re-analysis breaks segment_room_LINKS, but says nothing about adjustments — and links break VISIBLY (the room shows unlinked) whereas an adjustment re-attaches INVISIBLY to a different shape. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §467 documents a different, adjacent caveat (cross-scope id collision) and is not this.
findings.brands_affected: Eufy only in practice — image_segment_adjustments is written against the CV image_segments store, which only the Eufy CV segmentor populates.

findings.title: set_custom_segments' user-facing description is two features stale — it claims map-level scope and an uploaded-backdrop requirement that the layout + live-dims paths superseded
findings.what_code_does: services.yaml:2449-2457 describes set_custom_segments as rebuilding 'the map's custom segment set' with no mention of custom layouts at all, and states 'Requires a custom backdrop image (uploaded via upload_map_image) for the pixel dimensions'. The code at line 1667 targets the ACTIVE LAYOUT (auto-creating one), and lines 1673-1684 accept backdrop_width/backdrop_height from the call for a live-image-backed layout with no uploaded backdrop, refusing with no_custom_backdrop only when BOTH are missing. The in-file docstring (line 1645-1653) is likewise map-scoped in its first line ('REPLACE-ALL into the map's custom_segments store') before contradicting itself further down.
findings.reproduction: A user reads the service description in the HA Developer Tools > Actions UI (the only surface where a non-card caller learns this API), builds a script that authors segments, and reasonably concludes (a) that the write is map-scoped and layout-independent, and (b) that the call needs an uploaded backdrop. Both are wrong: the write silently targets whichever layout is active, and a live-backed layout works without an upload if backdrop_width/height are supplied — a parameter the description does not document at all.
findings.user_impact: Documentation precision only, but it is the load-bearing kind: the description is exactly what would have warned a caller about CUSTOM-1's implicit target, and it omits the two parameters that make the live-layout path usable. No runtime effect.
findings.guards_checked: SET_CUSTOM_SEGMENTS_SCHEMA (line 378-397) — does declare backdrop_width/backdrop_height, so the schema and the prose disagree; the card never reads services.yaml, so only script/automation authors are misled; docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.4 is accurate, so the drift is confined to the shipped service metadata and the handler's own first docstring line.
findings.doc_checked: custom_components/eufy_vacuum/services.yaml:2449-2478 versus docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.3-§10.4 (which correctly documents active-layout targeting, the per-layout custom_<id> variant, and the backdrop_width/height fallback). The dev doc is right and the user-facing service metadata is stale.
findings.brands_affected: Both.

clean_areas: _migrate_saved_zones (line 1388-1393) — verified idempotent and non-clobbering: the isinstance test seeds {} only when the key is absent or not a dict, and re-running never touches existing zones. Matches its docstring claim and the [ZONE-2] test at tests/integration/test_mapping_services.py:520.
