verdicts.reason: Executed against the shipped functions: a square scores exactly pi/4 regardless of size (so pi/4 is the attainable ceiling, not 1) and a rasterised disc scores LOWER than a square. Both docstring assertions are false. The perimeter it divides by is mask_perimeter's city-block edge count, which is what produces the (4/pi)^2 penalty on curves.
verdicts.evidence: Executed: compactness(1600, 160) = 0.7853981633974483 (40x40 square); compactness(10000, 400) = 0.7853981633974483 (100x100 square) — identical, confirming pi/4 is size-independent. Rasterised disc r=40: area 5025, mask_perimeter 324, compactness = 0.601528085821091. Source: segment_primitives.py:342-345 docstring 'Return the isoperimetric quotient (4piA / P^2).  Range 0-1; 1 = circle.' over `4.0 * math.pi * area / max(float(perimeter*perimeter), 1.0)`, where perimeter comes from mask_perimeter (:326-341), a 4-neighbour exposed-edge count. Module header lines 3-5 declare this module 'the recommended starting point when writing a new segmentor adapter'.

verdicts.reason: Executed: the function's output is plain chromaticity to float32 epsilon, so the Rec.709 luminance division provably cancels. The 1e-6 clamp that could break the cancellation is unreachable because the +1.0 floor guarantees a channel sum/luminance ratio of at least ~0.0117.
verdicts.evidence: Executed on np.array([[[10,20,30],[200,5,60]]], uint8): function output [[0.17460318, 0.33333331, 0.49206349], [0.75, 0.02238806, 0.22761194]] vs plain (rgb+1)/sum(rgb+1) [[0.17460318, 0.33333334, 0.49206349], [0.75, 0.02238806, 0.22761194]]; max abs difference 2.98e-08. Source: segment_primitives.py:526-534 — rgb_float = rgb.astype(np.float32) + 1.0; luminance = 0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B; luminance = np.maximum(luminance, 1.0); normalized = rgb_float / luminance[:,:,None]; channel_sum = np.maximum(normalized.sum(axis=2, keepdims=True), 1e-6); return normalized / channel_sum. Algebraically (rgb/L)/(sum(rgb)/L) = rgb/sum(rgb). Docstring says 'illumination-normalized chromaticity features'.

No arbiter exists, so 9 of 52 survivors reach synthesis with two different severities and no rule for picking one.

The two lenses applied DIFFERENT severity rubrics and neither noticed. The reproducer downgrades on consequence ('it never reaches the device and never alters the zone's geometry' - A4-CUSTOM-3; 'a display-only preference' - A5-FURNIS-2). The refuter downgrades on likelihood ('the trigger is a user-initiated delete... materially less surprising than the transient-triggered wrong-clean findings at HIGH here' - A6-ZONE-C-2; 'narrow enough that MEDIUM overstates it next to findings whose trigger is a routine transient' - A4-CUSTOM-5). The stated cap is consequence-based ('reaches the wire or destroys stored data'), so the refuter's likelihood-adjusted corrections sit outside the declared rubric. This is why 7 of the 9 conflicts fall along the same axis.

No CRITICAL was assigned anywhere in the 54, so the CRITICAL cap was never actually exercised. The boundary that was contested is HIGH/MEDIUM, and it has no written rule at all — which is what let the two rubrics diverge unremarked.
disagreements_resolved_by_evidence: A1-SERVIC-2 (path traversal) is the campaign's cleanest evidence-driven kill: both lenses independently executed the finder's exact construction and both got FileNotFoundError, and both independently identified the same off-by-one in the finder's normpath arithmetic. The reproducer went further than the refuter and found the mechanism boundary — a variant with an extra path component DOES write outside base_dir on Windows because Win32 canonicalizes '..' lexically before touching the filesystem, while POSIX resolves component-by-component and fails with ENOENT. That is the strongest single piece of verification work in the corpus.

A3-IMAGE--5's traversal sub-claim was independently refuted by BOTH lenses while the parent finding was confirmed, and both told the campaign to strike it before the fix ('one sub-claim is REFUTED and should be struck before this reaches a fix'). Correct handling of a partially-wrong finding — the filename-collision core survived, the wrong security framing did not.

A2-POLYGO-1's compounding-drift claim was independently re-executed by both lenses over 8 round-trip cycles. Their numbers differ by exactly one cycle of offset (refuter 20.50->21.80, reproducer 20.3->21.6), which is positive evidence that both really ran it rather than transcribing the finder's table.

A6-ZONE-C-3's load-bearing claim (the map_version invalidation key specified by the design doc does not exist) was settled by both lenses independently running the same repo-wide grep and both getting zero hits in code and exactly one hit in docs. Duplicated, but a zero-hit grep run twice is the right kind of duplication for a claim of absence.
duplicate_effort: The two lenses executed almost exactly the same set of tests. Refuter executed on 11 findings; reproducer on 12; 11 of those overlap. The only finding the reproducer executed that the refuter did not is A7-ROBORO-2. The refuter executed nothing the reproducer did not. The second lens bought one new measurement for eleven repeated ones.

On A2-POLYGO-6 and A2-POLYGO-7 the two lenses report identical output to the last digit (compactness 0.7853981633974483 and 0.601528..., max abs difference 2.98e-08). These are LOW, no-runtime-defect docstring findings that the finder had already executed and shown its arithmetic for. Both lenses spent an execution each re-deriving a settled number.

A2-POLYGO-4 (both report bbox (100,100)-(303,303), area 41209 px), A7-ROBORO-1, A7-ROBORO-5 and A7-ROBORO-6 were each executed twice with byte-identical results and identical conclusions. On A1-SERVIC-7 both lenses independently discovered that the '2 hits' grep count is a .claude/worktrees clone artifact and both wrote it up separately.

Effort was allocated inversely to stakes. The 12 executed findings cluster entirely in the two pure-function modules (polygon-math, roborock-raw-map) — the code that is easy to call. Zero findings in custom-layouts, furnished-render or zone-crud-dispatch were executed by either lens.
result.estimated_value_added: "Low-to-moderate: roughly 3-6% of campaign value, and zero change to any survive/kill outcome. Concretely I produced: one empirical cross-lens contradiction resolved by running both fixtures (A7-ROBORO-7); nine severity conflicts that the outcome counts structurally hide; one named rubric divergence (likelihood-adjusted vs consequence-based) that explains 7 of those 9; two root-cause merges that would erase a distinct consequence if performed naively; one HIGH destructive finding (A2-POLYGO-2) that neither lens executed despite it being a three-line test; and the measurement that 42 of 54 findings (78%) were adjudicated by two source-reading passes rather than by any reproduction. That is about one triage session's worth of correction to the fix ordering, not a re-run of anything. The honest framing is that the two-lens structure worked well enough that the third layer found process defects rather than wrong answers — which is a good result for the campaign and a weak result for me."
findings_strengthened: A4-CUSTOM-2: the reproducer alone noticed that in the zero-layout state the segments_store is ALSO the throwaway {}, so get_map_segments serves segments=[] and there is nothing to link — narrowing the writable surface to the mascot dock anchor and correcting HIGH->MEDIUM. The refuter left it HIGH without spotting this. Genuine new reasoning, not restatement.

A7-ROBORO-2: the reproducer measured 0.0744 s for a 700x700 raster and used it to strike the finder's 'comfortably into multiple seconds' claim. The refuter confirmed the same finding without ever testing the cost claim, implicitly ratifying a figure that was wrong by roughly an order of magnitude. This is the clearest case of the reproducer lens earning its cost.

A2-POLYGO-8: the refuter alone caught that a sub-claim is overstated — a primitive with an unrecognised `type` in ISOLATION leaves `drew` False and returns [], so it IS counted in `skipped`; it is only silent when mixed with a valid primitive. The reproducer repeated the finder's unqualified version ('An unrecognised type matches no branch and raises nothing at all'). Clearest case of the refuter lens earning its cost.

A3-IMAGE--2: the reproducer alone flagged that the finder's second entry path (Roborock/noop wiping segments on first analyze) is implausible, since it requires an uploaded PNG plus pre-existing CV segments on a noop_fallback adapter. The refuter accepted both paths. The Eufy engine_exception path survives intact.

A2-POLYGO-5 and A3-IMAGE--1: both lenses independently found the segmentor's `segments.sort(key=lambda item: (-area_pixels, ...))` at segmentor.py:1414/1485, which the finders had not cited. That sort is what turns 'per-run ordinal' into 'Nth-largest blob' and is the actual mechanism of id instability — a real addition, found twice.
findings_weakened_or_killed: A1-SERVIC-2 killed by both lenses on executed evidence. The residual true observation (uncaught FileNotFoundError on a '/'-containing map_id) was correctly routed to A3-IMAGE--5 rather than dropped.
A5-FURNIS-2 killed by survival rule after a 1-1 label split; see disagreements_averaged_away. The kill is defensible but the substance behind it was never ruled on.

Both lenses agreed on exactly two severity downgrades: A5-FURNIS-1 HIGH->MEDIUM (parity with A1-SERVIC-5, which covers a superset of eight services) and A5-FURNIS-3 MEDIUM->LOW (no consumer reads per-room viewports today). Both are well-argued and mutually corroborated.

Sub-claim corrections that survived into the record: the A3-IMAGE--5 POSIX traversal claim (struck by both), the A2-POLYGO-8 unknown-type claim (struck by refuter), the A7-ROBORO-2 cost claim (struck by reproducer), the A3-IMAGE--2 noop-adapter path (struck by reproducer), and the A3-IMAGE--10 title count — the refuter noted it is FIVE of five services undeclared in services.yaml, not four.
independence_failures: The reproducer's A5-FURNIS-2 verdict rests its rationale on the FINDER'S OWN concession rather than on anything it tested: 'the finder itself frames it as a note against the FURNIS-1 fix rather than a defect.' Its evidence block then re-quotes the finder's own line range and scenario verbatim ('mapping_services.py:2242-2257: `map_id = call.data.get("map_id"); if not map_id: try: map_id = get_active_map_id(...)`') and adds no test the finder had not already run. That is the finder's reasoning reflected back with a severity label attached.

The reproducer's A4-CUSTOM-6 verdict claims independence by cross-reference: 'Same defect as A2-POLYGO-5, verified independently.' Its evidence is the same set of citations used in POLYGO-5's own verdicts (segmentor.py:1289/1474 mint, 1414/1485 sort, _apply_segment_adjustments:769-770). Agreeing with a sibling verdict is not an independent test of the claim.

On A2-POLYGO-2 — a HIGH, silent-destruction-of-stored-data finding — NEITHER lens executed anything, and both evidence blocks are the finder's own line citations restated (reproducer: '`if PIL_Image is None or np is None: return []` — same `[]` as lines 309 and 313'). The finder HAD executed it. I re-ran it in three lines: setting segment_primitives.PIL_Image = None makes rasterize_primitives return [] for a valid rect, byte-identical to the empty-input return. Both lenses accepted the finder's execution on the highest-stakes destructive claim in that area while separately re-deriving the settled arithmetic of two LOW docstring findings.

The whole of zone-crud-dispatch, custom-layouts and furnished-render (21 findings, including three wire-reaching HIGHs) was adjudicated by two passes of source reading. For A6-ZONE-C-1 in particular, the finding's load-bearing arithmetic (the -400mm vs 3000mm projection of one stored rect against two different maps' correspondences) was never recomputed by either lens; both restated the code path. That arithmetic is checkable with two synthetic correspondence sets and normalized_rects_to_mm.
result.recommended_future_use: "Do NOT run a meta-verifier as a per-subsystem agent — it is the wrong shape for the value it produces, and nothing it found changed an outcome. Everything material in this report is mechanically computable by the harness at ~zero token cost. Add three assertions instead, and skip the third layer entirely: (1) SEVERITY CONFLICT FLAG — emit a warning whenever the two lenses' severity_correction fields disagree (would have surfaced all 9 conflicts and, by their shared direction, the rubric divergence); (2) UNVERIFIED-PREMISE GATE — refuse a bare CONFIRMED on any finding whose confidence is 'needs-runtime-check' unless a verdict records an executed check; force it into a distinct CONFIRMED-SOURCE-ONLY state and auto-route it to the hardware run (would have caught all 7); (3) EXECUTION DIFF — flag any finding where both lenses executed and reported divergent results, or where NEITHER executed despite severity >= HIGH (would have surfaced ROBORO-7 and POLYGO-2). Also worth one line in the verifier prompts: state the HIGH/MEDIUM rule explicitly as consequence-based, since the CRITICAL cap was never exercised and the boundary that actually got contested has no written rule. If a meta layer is ever run again, run it ONCE at end-of-campaign across all eleven subsystems looking for cross-subsystem rubric drift — not per subsystem, where there is too little variance to measure."
routed_back_for_reproduction: A7-ROBORO-7 — RESOLVE THE FIXTURE QUESTION (I already did; confirm before fixing). The two lenses executed the same nominal test and reported opposite results: refuter 'decode returned None (width read as 0 tripped :111), confirming the case is not reachable by accident'; reproducer 'decode returned {width: 200, height: 150, top: 30000, ...}'. Both are right about their own fixture. I ran both: with header_len=20 and height/width placed at offsets 12/16 the decode returns a plausible raster with top=30000 (the data_len field read as a coordinate); with header_len=16 it returns width=4, height=4, top=1048578 == 2 | (16<<16), i.e. the type and header_len int16s read as one coordinate. A naive fixture returns None. So the correct characterisation is CONSTRUCTIBLE BUT NOT ACCIDENTAL — which is neither lens's stated conclusion. The fix (>= 24 not >= 16) is unchanged; the priority is lower than 'constructible' and higher than 'unreachable'.

A2-POLYGO-2 — HIGH, silent destruction of an authored layout, never executed by either lens. It is a three-line test (set segment_primitives.PIL_Image = None; call rasterize_primitives on a valid rect; observe []). I confirmed the sentinel collision holds. What still needs reproduction is the CALLER half nobody ran: drive _handle_set_custom_segments with a populated layout and a stubbed-out PIL to confirm the unconditional overwrite plus async_save actually commits the empty store — this is exactly the campaign's known harness hazard (a plausible sequence is not the real one), and the destructive claim rests on the commit, not on the [].

A6-ZONE-C-1 — HIGH and wire-reaching, adjudicated by source reading only. Recompute the projection with two synthetic correspondence sets through normalized_rects_to_mm to confirm that (a) the same normalized rect maps to materially different mm rectangles and (b) the residual gate genuinely passes on the wrong-map fit. The residual-gate claim is the part that makes this unstoppable, and it was asserted by both lenses without being run.

The seven 'needs-runtime-check' findings (A2-POLYGO-5, A3-IMAGE--8, A3-IMAGE--9, A4-CUSTOM-6, A5-FURNIS-5, A7-ROBORO-4, A6-ZONE-C-6) were all CONFIRMED by both lenses with no runtime check performed. The reproducer hedged correctly on five of them ('device/image data I do not have'); the refuter confirmed several flatly. These should carry a distinct state into the hardware run rather than entering the fix queue as CONFIRMED. A7-ROBORO-4 in particular is a MEDIUM whose entire impact is conditional on the HA roborock parser's ImageConfig trim being nonzero — and the shipped geometry_drift diagnostic settles it with one 'Download diagnostics' on the real S6.

A3-IMAGE--9 and A4-CUSTOM-1 assert concurrency defects across an await that nobody reproduced. Both are defensible as structural claims (the await is real), but neither lens constructed the interleaving, and A4-CUSTOM-1's multi-client scenario is the destructive one.

LEAD ONLY, not a finding, and must not be accepted on this pass's authority: the A1-SERVIC-2 reproducer found that the traversal DOES write outside base_dir on a Windows host and scoped it away as 'every supported HA deployment' being POSIX. That scoping is an assumption stated in a verdict, not a verified fact about this project's support matrix. One line of confirmation would close it; if any supported deployment is Windows, the killed finding is live there.

MERGE HAZARD, for the synthesis pass. The refuter flagged 'dedupe downstream' on A4-CUSTOM-6 naming A2-POLYGO-5 and A3-IMAGE--1 as one root cause. Merging those three naively ERASES a distinct consequence: POLYGO-5 and CUSTOM-6 both concern image_segment_adjustments and are correctly display-only ('nothing physical goes wrong'), whereas IMAGE--1 concerns segment_room_links and is ACTUATING — tapping the polygon calls toggleRoomEnabled for the stale room and the vacuum cleans a room the user did not point at. Two of the three say display-only, so a majority-flavoured merge would drop the wire-reaching consequence. Same hazard on the A1-SERVIC-1 / A6-ZONE-C-6 pair: SERVIC-1's consequence is stranded-unreachable geometry after a vendor rename, ZONE-C-6 adds phantom buckets surfacing in get_vacuum_maps_summary from a mere typo and bucket-minting on the read-only clean paths. Distinct consequences, one mechanism.
unresolved_claims: Nine severity rulings stand unreconciled (listed under disagreements_averaged_away). Four of these are HIGH/MEDIUM boundary calls on findings that will drive fix ordering: A6-ZONE-C-2 (refuter M, reproducer H), A4-CUSTOM-2 (refuter H, reproducer M), A4-CUSTOM-3 (refuter H, reproducer M), plus A5-FURNIS-2's kill-vs-LOW.

A7-ROBORO-4's actual impact is unresolved by construction, and both lenses said so honestly: the offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame depends on the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim, which is not in this repo. The finding is CONFIRMED at MEDIUM with a consequence chain (overlays offset, wrong room named on click, displaced physical zone clean) that is entirely conditional on a premise nobody could test. The reproducer correctly noted the finder's 0.39 m figure is 'a worked hypothetical with an assumed T=50, not a measurement'.

A5-FURNIS-5's MEDIUM rests on the rendered map extent changing across a re-map, which the reproducer explicitly could not settle ('device behaviour I cannot settle from source') while leaving the severity unchanged; the refuter downgraded to LOW citing the same unverified premise. Same premise, opposite handling.

A6-ZONE-C-6's Roborock trigger — that the select entity's state actually changes when a map is renamed in the vendor app — is unverified by both lenses. The typo variant needs no rename and is solid, so the finding survives regardless, but the headline scenario (all zones and layouts stranded after a rename) does not.

The verdict vocabulary itself is unresolved. 'CONFIRMED' is used interchangeably for 'the defect occurs' and 'the code reads as the finder described', and A7-ROBORO-4 and A5-FURNIS-5 sit entirely in the second sense. Nothing in the artifact distinguishes them, so synthesis cannot tell a reproduced defect from a verified code reading without re-reading every evidence block.
result.verification_coverage: "The supplied per-area table is HONEST and I confirmed it against the verdicts rather than trusting it. All 54 findings carry exactly two verdicts, one per lens, and the per-area counts reconcile exactly: service-surface 7 (SERVIC-1..7), polygon-math 8, image-lifecycle 11 (IMAGE--1..11, with --11 filed out of order between --7 and --8), custom-layouts 7, furnished-render 6, zone-crud-dispatch 8, roborock-raw-map 7 = 54, and 108 verdicts with zero unjudged. The outcome counts also reconcile: 52 survivors listed + 2 in the killed array = 54, with A5-FURNIS-2 correctly appearing in both the killed and split arrays (killed by the survival rule after a 1-1 label split). Neither lens thinned out on any AREA. But coverage by verdict count conceals a severe imbalance in verification DEPTH: only 12 of 54 findings (22%) were adjudicated with any executed code by either lens, and those 12 cluster entirely in the two pure-function modules — polygon-math (5 of 8) and roborock-raw-map (5 of 7), plus SERVIC-2 and IMAGE--5. Zero findings in custom-layouts (7), furnished-render (6) or zone-crud-dispatch (8) were executed by either lens. 42 of 54 findings (78%), including three wire-reaching HIGHs, were adjudicated by two independent passes of source reading — which is real verification, but is not what 'reproducer' names, and means that for most of the corpus the second lens differed from the first in emphasis rather than in method."
